questions.key: Leverage the Retail API through Model Garden to implement product recommendations, optimized search, and promotion optimization.

questions.stem: A financial institution wants to develop a highly accurate model to predict customer churn. The customer data, which includes both numerical transaction history and categorical demographic information, is already stored in BigQuery. The data analytics team is highly proficient in SQL but has limited experience with advanced machine learning model development. The goal is to leverage a sophisticated tree-based model to achieve high predictive accuracy, surpassing simpler linear models, while minimizing the need for extensive ML engineering expertise. What should you do?
questions.key: Use BigQuery ML to train a BOOSTED_TREE_CLASSIFIER model on the customer data in BigQuery.

questions.stem:
A large e-commerce company processes millions of product images and their associated text descriptions daily. Multiple data science and ML engineering teams collaborate on developing recommendation systems, visual search, and content moderation models. The company requires a robust solution for managing these multi-modal datasets, ensuring full auditability and reproducibility of features used in models. New data is ingested daily, and feature definitions evolve frequently. The solution must support efficient versioning of both raw data and derived features, provide clear lineage from raw data to features, enable cross-team feature sharing, and accommodate high-throughput processing for daily updates, all while maintaining cost-effectiveness.

What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a data pipeline using Dataflow to process raw images and text from Cloud Storage, and then store the extracted and transformed features in Vertex AI Feature Store with versioning enabled. Orchestrate this pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines to track lineage and automate daily updates.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs to predict customer churn to proactively retain high-value clients. The customer data, including historical transaction patterns, account activity, and demographic information, is stored in BigQuery. The data contains both numerical and categorical features, and preliminary analysis suggests complex, non-linear relationships between these features and churn. The data analytics team is proficient in SQL but has limited machine learning engineering expertise. The solution must provide high accuracy, effectively handle the non-linear relationships, and offer reasonable interpretability for business stakeholders to understand the drivers of churn. What should you do?
questions.key: Use BigQuery ML to train a Boosted Trees Classifier model on the existing BigQuery dataset.

questions.stem: A financial institution stores millions of daily transaction records in BigQuery. They need to implement a low-code solution to identify potentially fraudulent transactions. Historical data indicates that fraudulent activities are extremely rare and often lack consistent, clear labels, making traditional supervised classification challenging. The solution must be capable of handling a high-dimensional dataset and facilitate rapid iteration and deployment by a team with limited deep machine learning expertise. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a BigQuery ML Autoencoder model on the transaction data.

questions.stem: A financial institution is developing a critical machine learning model for fraud detection. Multiple data science and engineering teams collaborate on this project. Due to strict regulatory requirements, the institution must ensure complete data versioning and lineage for all raw data, preprocessed features, model artifacts, and predictions. Any model prediction must be traceable back to the exact version of raw data, feature engineering logic, and model training run. The solution needs to support collaborative development, automate the ML lifecycle for reproducibility, and provide robust audit trails. The institution requires a cost-effective and highly auditable solution. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement an MLOps platform using Vertex AI Pipelines to orchestrate the end-to-end ML workflow, storing raw data in Cloud Storage with versioning enabled, managing processed features in Vertex AI Feature Store, registering model artifacts and metadata in Vertex AI Model Registry, and deploying models via Vertex AI Endpoints. Integrate Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace to capture detailed execution logs and lineage information for all pipeline steps.

questions.stem: A large media company manages an extensive archive of multimedia content, including millions of images and videos. The company needs to implement a robust, low-code solution to automatically detect inappropriate content (e.g., explicit imagery) within new uploads to ensure compliance and brand safety. Additionally, they want to enhance their internal content discovery system, allowing editors to semantically search the vast multimedia archive based on content descriptions and visual elements, without requiring extensive ML expertise from the editors. The solution must be cost-efficient and minimize operational overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vision API for explicit content detection and metadata extraction from images, and store this metadata in BigQuery. Then, use BigQuery ML's AI.EMBED function to generate embeddings from the extracted metadata, enabling semantic search for content discovery.

questions.stem:
A large media company is launching a new initiative to develop multi-modal AI models for advanced content moderation and transcription services. They possess petabytes of raw, unstructured video and audio files currently residing on disparate on-premises network attached storage (NAS) systems. The company plans to migrate this extensive data to Google Cloud, aiming to leverage Vertex AI for model training.

The solution must ensure efficient and scalable access to the raw data for all future multi-modal model development, minimize redundant data movement during training workflows, and support clear versioning of the raw data for reproducibility. The immediate goal is to prepare these raw files for ingestion into Vertex AI datasets, enabling distinct, versioned datasets for various training experiments. What should you do?
questions.key: Migrate all raw video and audio files to separate Cloud Storage buckets, maintaining a logical folder structure (e.g., /projectA/video/raw/, /projectA/audio/raw/). For each dataset version, generate a manifest file (CSV or JSONL) containing the Cloud Storage URIs of the respective raw files and any associated labels or metadata. Subsequently, use these manifest files to create new, versioned Vertex AI Datasets for video and audio, which can then be directly referenced by Vertex AI training jobs.

questions.stem: A retail company stores its transactional customer data, including historical purchases and customer demographics, in BigQuery. They need to predict Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) for marketing segmentation using a low-code machine learning approach. The solution must automate complex feature engineering steps, such as aggregating historical purchase data to calculate Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) values, and encoding various categorical features, before training the model. The final model should be easily deployed for predictions without requiring extensive ML engineering expertise. What should you do?
questions.key: Use BigQuery SQL to perform all necessary feature engineering, including RFM calculations and categorical encoding, storing the results in a new BigQuery table. Then, create an AutoML Tables dataset from this prepared BigQuery table and train a regression model.

questions.stem: A data science team is developing a critical recommendation model using Vertex AI Pipelines. They are iteratively experimenting with dozens of different feature engineering techniques, model architectures, and hyperparameter configurations, resulting in numerous pipeline runs. The team needs an efficient way to track and compare the performance metrics (e.g., AUC, precision, recall) and associated artifacts (e.g., trained model files, evaluation reports, input datasets) from all these runs to identify the best performing model. Manually sifting through individual pipeline run logs and Cloud Storage buckets is becoming unsustainable and error-prone. The solution must support systematic comparison to select the optimal model for production deployment. What should you do?
questions.key: Associate each Vertex AI Pipeline run with a Vertex AI Experiment and log all relevant metrics, parameters, and artifact URIs within the experiment run. Then, use the Vertex AI Experiments interface to compare performance metrics, parameters, and artifact lineage across all experiment runs.

questions.stem:
A retail company stores its extensive customer transaction data, including purchasing history, demographics, and browsing behavior, in BigQuery. The data includes both numerical and categorical features. The company wants to predict Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) to better target marketing campaigns. They have a data science team proficient in SQL, but with limited traditional machine learning expertise, and they need a solution that offers higher predictive accuracy than a simple linear regression model. The solution must be cost-effective and integrate seamlessly with their existing BigQuery data.

What should you do to build and deploy a CLV prediction model?
questions.key: Use BigQuery ML to create a BOOSTED_TREE_REGRESSOR model, train it directly on the BigQuery data using SQL, and then use SQL to evaluate its performance and generate predictions.

questions.stem: A manufacturing company operates an automated assembly line that produces thousands of components daily. They need to implement a system to automatically identify and classify custom surface defects on these components using images captured from the line. The company has accumulated a large dataset of over 100,000 images, meticulously labeled with various defect types. The internal team has limited machine learning engineering expertise, and the solution must be deployed quickly with minimal code development, while also being cost-efficient and scalable to handle continuous image streams. What should you do?
questions.key: Use AutoML Vision to create and train a custom image classification model using the labeled dataset, then deploy it to a Vertex AI Endpoint for online predictions.

questions.stem: A large call center needs to automatically transcribe thousands of hours of customer service call recordings to identify common issues, agent performance keywords, and customer sentiment. The company has a limited team of data analysts with SQL proficiency but minimal machine learning engineering expertise. They require a low-code solution that can accurately process audio data, integrate with their existing data warehouse in BigQuery for further analysis, and minimize manual transcription efforts to reduce operational costs. What should you do?
questions.key: Use AutoML Speech (part of Vertex AI) to train a custom speech-to-text model on their call recordings and then integrate the transcriptions into BigQuery for analysis.

questions.stem: A large media company receives millions of user-generated images and text comments daily. They need to automatically detect and flag inappropriate content across both modalities to maintain platform safety and comply with regulations. The solution must be deployed quickly, require minimal machine learning development effort, and scale to handle high volumes of incoming data efficiently. The company's data is primarily stored in BigQuery and Cloud Storage. What should you do?
questions.key: Use the Vision API for explicit content detection on images stored in Cloud Storage and use BigQuery ML's AI.CLASSIFY function to categorize text comments for inappropriateness directly within BigQuery.

questions.stem:
A large healthcare organization is developing a patient risk prediction model on Google Cloud, involving two distinct data science teams. Team A is responsible for preprocessing sensitive patient health information (PHI) and creating features, while Team B builds and trains the machine learning model. Regulatory compliance mandates strict data versioning, explicit lineage tracking from raw data to trained model, and full reproducibility of any model prediction. Data sharing between teams must be controlled and consistent. The organization needs a solution that ensures features are versioned, shared efficiently, and traceable to the exact data used for model training, minimizing operational overhead.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Implement a data processing pipeline using Dataflow to transform raw PHI into features, storing the processed features in BigQuery. Publish these features to Vertex AI Feature Store, ensuring versioning. Orchestrate the entire workflow, from data ingestion to model training, using Vertex AI Pipelines, which registers the trained model and its metadata, including links to the specific feature versions from Vertex AI Feature Store, in Vertex AI Model Registry.

questions.stem: A data science team of five engineers is tasked with rapidly prototyping a novel deep learning model architecture for image classification. They need to collaboratively develop and iterate on the model within a shared Jupyter notebook environment, allowing all five team members to simultaneously edit and execute code. The prototyping involves processing a large image dataset stored in Cloud Storage. The primary goals are to maximize real-time collaboration, accelerate iteration cycles, and maintain efficient resource utilization for exploratory development. What should you do?
questions.key: Provision a Colab Enterprise instance for the team and share the Jupyter notebook.

questions.stem: A large media company needs to process petabytes of raw video and audio content daily to extract machine learning features. These features include speech-to-text transcripts, detected objects in video frames, and identified audio events. Multiple ML engineering teams will use these features to train and serve a variety of models, such as content recommendation, moderation, and search. The solution must be highly scalable, handle complex transformations on unstructured data, ensure data quality, and provide a centralized, versioned repository for features to promote reusability across teams for both training and online inference. Cost-efficiency for large-scale processing is also a key consideration. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a Dataflow pipeline using Apache Beam to perform the large-scale, complex transformations for extracting features from raw video and audio. Store the processed features in BigQuery for structured data or Cloud Storage for unstructured/semi-structured data. Then, ingest these features into Vertex AI Feature Store to centralize, version, and serve them for training and online inference across all ML teams.

questions.stem: A financial institution is expanding its machine learning operations and needs to provide secure, collaborative, and high-performance development environments for several data science teams. Team A requires high-performance Spark kernels for large-scale data processing and model training. Team B needs a fully managed notebook environment with integrated source code version control. Team C prioritizes real-time collaborative editing for joint model development. All environments must adhere to strict financial industry security and compliance standards, including network isolation from the public internet and comprehensive access control. What should you do to meet these diverse requirements while maintaining high security?
questions.key: Provision Vertex AI Workbench instances for all teams. For Team A, configure the Workbench instances to connect to Dataproc clusters for Spark kernel execution. For Team B, leverage Vertex AI Workbench's managed JupyterLab environment with integrated Git for version control. For Team C, utilize Colab Enterprise for real-time collaboration, accessible from Vertex AI Workbench. Implement fine-grained IAM roles, configure private services access for network isolation, and integrate with Security Command Center for threat detection.

questions.stem: A large healthcare organization is developing several machine learning models to predict patient outcomes and identify disease risks. Different ML teams within the organization are independently developing and using various features derived from sensitive patient health information (PHI) stored in BigQuery. Features are constantly evolving, and there is a critical need to ensure consistent feature definitions, track feature lineage from raw data, and enable efficient, versioned sharing of these features across all teams. The solution must support reproducibility of model training, adhere to strict data privacy regulations, and minimize operational overhead for feature management. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI Feature Store to centralize and serve versioned features. Implement Dataflow pipelines to extract, transform, and load features from BigQuery into Vertex AI Feature Store, ensuring each feature version is linked to its source data and transformation logic. Teams will consume features from the Feature Store, ensuring consistent definitions and access control.

questions.stem:
An e-commerce company is developing a new fraud detection model. They are running numerous experiments to fine-tune model hyperparameters, needing to track and compare the performance metrics, parameters, and generated artifacts for each experiment run. Once an optimal model is identified and deployed to production, the company requires a fully auditable record of its lineage, including the exact version of the training dataset used, all preprocessing steps applied, and the specific model artifact. This auditing capability is critical for compliance and debugging. The entire process must be automated within their existing Vertex AI environment.

What should you do to meet these requirements efficiently?
questions.key: Orchestrate the model training and evaluation using Vertex AI Pipelines. Configure each hyperparameter tuning iteration as a distinct pipeline run within a Vertex AI Experiment. Rely on Vertex AI Pipelines' native capabilities to automatically log all input datasets, preprocessing steps, and model artifacts to Vertex ML Metadata for auditable lineage.

questions.stem: A healthcare provider has deployed a diagnostic machine learning model on Vertex AI Prediction to assist in early disease detection. The model demonstrates high overall accuracy, but internal reviews and feedback from clinicians raise concerns about its decision-making process for rare conditions and specific minority patient demographics. There is a critical need to understand why the model produces certain predictions for these sensitive cases to identify potential biases or unintended correlations that could lead to misdiagnosis or unfair treatment. The solution must provide insight into the model's internal reasoning without compromising patient data privacy. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Explainable AI to generate feature attributions for model predictions, focusing analysis on predictions made for patients belonging to rare condition groups and minority demographics.

questions.stem: A financial services company uses a critical fraud detection model deployed on Vertex AI Prediction. Recently, the model's performance metrics, specifically precision and recall for detecting new fraud attempts, have shown a sudden and significant degradation, dropping by 15% over the past week. Furthermore, internal anomaly detection systems have flagged unusual patterns in the model's predictions for a specific subset of customer transactions, exhibiting an unexpected increase in false negatives. The data engineering team confirms no significant changes in the upstream data pipelines. The company suspects a potential data poisoning attack targeting the training data, aiming to degrade the model's effectiveness, and requires an immediate and robust solution to detect and mitigate such threats while maintaining high availability. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to detect data drift by comparing serving data distributions against a golden dataset, and prediction drift for output anomalies. Establish a Vertex AI Pipeline for continuous model evaluation using a separate, securely curated test dataset, triggering alerts in Cloud Monitoring for performance degradation. In case of confirmed data poisoning, roll back to a known good model version from Vertex AI Model Registry, and retrain the model with a verified clean dataset.

questions.stem:
Your organization stores a dataset of historical customer service conversations in BigQuery. You need to fine-tune a Gemini foundation model on this data to improve task accuracy for domain-specific query responses. You want to accomplish this directly in BigQuery by using standard SQL without exporting the data or managing custom training scripts. You have already created a BigQuery Cloud resource connection.

What configuration and SQL statement must you use to successfully run the supervised fine-tuning job?
questions.key: Grant the Vertex AI Service Agent role to the Cloud resource connection's service account, and execute a CREATE MODEL statement that specifies REMOTE WITH CONNECTION, sets ENDPOINT to the target Gemini model, and includes an AS SELECT clause pointing to the prompt and label columns in the BigQuery table.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose demand forecasting service helps planners replenish stores. Monitoring shows that evaluated model candidates wait several days for manual release. Cloud Build already tests training-code changes, and an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow trains candidates and evaluates them on held-out sales data. Your team is connecting code integration and continuous training to automated releases. You want to minimize changes to the existing workflows while minimizing the risk of promoting candidates with inadequate forecast accuracy. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Extend Cloud Build to test code changes and invoke the existing Agent Platform Pipelines workflow. Automatically deploy the resulting candidate only after its held-out evaluation meets the forecast-quality release thresholds.

questions.stem: A data science team at a large enterprise heavily relies on Apache Spark for extensive data preprocessing and feature engineering, which are critical steps before training their machine learning models on Google Cloud. The team needs a collaborative Jupyter-like environment that allows multiple data scientists to work simultaneously on the same notebook, seamlessly integrate with their existing Spark workflows, and automatically manage the underlying compute resources for Spark jobs. The solution must also support easy integration with version control systems and minimize operational overhead for cluster management. What is the most efficient solution to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Use Colab Enterprise with Spark kernels, linking notebooks to a Git repository for version control.

questions.stem:
A large financial institution is developing a critical machine learning model for real-time fraud detection. Due to stringent regulatory compliance requirements, the organization must ensure complete auditability and reproducibility of all data, code, and model artifacts used in the development and deployment lifecycle. Multiple teams, including data engineers, ML engineers, and MLOps specialists, collaborate on this project. They need a solution that provides robust versioning for raw input data, intermediate preprocessed datasets, and all trained model artifacts. The solution must also offer clear lineage tracking from the raw data through preprocessing and model training to final model deployment, enabling any past model prediction to be fully traceable back to its exact data and code origins. Furthermore, the development environment needs to support collaborative experimentation and transparent tracking of all ML experiments for reproducibility. The organization needs to minimize operational overhead while meeting these strict governance and collaboration demands.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Implement a solution using Cloud Storage with object versioning for raw data, BigQuery for structured data preprocessing and storage, Dataflow for complex data transformations, Vertex AI Pipelines for end-to-end workflow orchestration and lineage tracking, Vertex AI Model Registry for model artifact management, and Vertex AI Experiments for collaborative experiment tracking.

questions.stem:
A large financial institution has two separate ML engineering teams collaborating on a new fraud detection system. One team is developing a large language model (LLM) using PyTorch on custom training jobs to analyze transaction narratives, while the other is building an image generation model with JAX for anomaly detection in scanned documents. Both teams need to iteratively develop, evaluate, and compare the performance and quality of their generative models. The organization requires a unified, collaborative platform to track experiment runs, visualize training metrics (like loss curves, generated outputs over time), and compare different model versions and hyperparameter configurations to ensure reproducibility and facilitate cross-team insights. The solution must support both PyTorch and JAX frameworks and scale for large model development.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Configure both teams to train their generative models using Vertex AI training clusters, log all experiment parameters, metrics, and generated artifacts to Vertex AI Experiments, and centralize the visualization and comparison of these experiments using a shared Vertex AI TensorBoard instance.

questions.stem: A healthcare company is developing a machine learning model for early disease diagnosis based on tabular patient data. Due to strict regulatory compliance and the need for medical practitioners to understand and trust the model's reasoning for each diagnosis, interpretability is a critical, non-negotiable requirement. The model's predictions must be easily explainable, not just interpretable post-hoc. The data scientists have a foundational understanding of ML concepts and data workflows. They need to train a model on Google Cloud that inherently offers high transparency and can be integrated into a robust, automated MLOps pipeline. What should you do?
questions.key: Develop a custom training application using Scikit-learn for a Logistic Regression model within a Vertex AI Training Pipeline, specifying n1-standard-4 machine types for training, and configure the pipeline to upload the resulting model to Vertex AI Model Registry.

questions.stem: A small marketing agency wants to develop a customer churn prediction model for its clients. The agency has various tabular datasets, each up to 1 million rows and 100 features, stored in Cloud Storage. The team consists primarily of data analysts with limited machine learning engineering experience, so they require a solution that minimizes coding effort and allows for rapid model development and iteration. The solution must be scalable and allow the data analysts to manage the model training process without deep ML expertise. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI AutoML Tabular to train the customer churn prediction model.

questions.stem: A data science team has developed a custom image classification model for product categorization. They are using Vertex AI Custom Training for experimentation and have successfully trained several model versions, each with different architectures and hyperparameters. The team needs to manage these model versions effectively, including tracking their metadata, ensuring reproducibility, and preparing them for seamless deployment to production for A/B testing and future serving. They want an automated solution that integrates directly with Vertex AI's deployment capabilities after each successful training run. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure a Vertex AI Training Pipeline to encapsulate the custom training job and automatically upload the resulting model to Vertex AI Model Registry after training.

questions.stem: A leading healthcare organization is developing a new diagnostic model using a large tabular dataset of patient health records. This model will assist clinicians in identifying early indicators of a specific disease. Due to strict regulatory compliance requirements and the need for clinical trust, the model must provide human-understandable explanations for every individual prediction. The development team also requires an automated and repeatable training process to ensure consistency and auditability for future model updates. What should you do?
questions.key: Develop the model using the XGBoost framework, implement custom training code, and orchestrate the training, evaluation, and model registration process using Vertex AI Pipelines.

questions.stem: A large financial institution has a mature ML development ecosystem that relies heavily on Kubernetes for orchestrating complex multi-step ML workflows and uses custom Python scripts for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. They need to migrate this entire workflow to Google Cloud. The primary goal is to maintain maximum control over their custom training code and environment while reusing their existing Kubernetes-based orchestration practices and tooling as much as possible to minimize refactoring efforts and leverage familiar patterns. The solution must support GPU-accelerated training for deep learning models. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement the ML workflows using Vertex AI Pipelines, defining each step as a custom container that executes your Python scripts, and configure the pipeline steps to use appropriate GPU-enabled machine types.

questions.stem:
A financial services company operates two data science teams that collaborate on a critical fraud detection model. Team A is responsible for preparing and curating raw transaction data, storing it in BigQuery. Team B consumes this data, performs extensive feature engineering, trains the model, and manages its lifecycle. The company operates in a highly regulated industry, requiring strict data lineage, auditability of all data and feature versions used for model training, and the ability to reproduce any model's results based on specific historical data and feature sets. Both teams need to efficiently share and access these versioned data and features while maintaining consistency.

What should you do to ensure robust data and feature versioning, lineage, and auditability for both teams?
questions.key: Implement a system where Team A manages raw data versions in BigQuery using partitioned tables and snapshotting, and Team B uses Vertex AI Feature Store to store and version engineered features derived from BigQuery, linking feature versions to their upstream data sources.

questions.stem: A data science team is developing a critical fraud detection model within Vertex AI. They have executed numerous training pipeline runs, each exploring different feature engineering techniques, model architectures, and hyperparameter configurations. Each run generates various artifacts, including preprocessed datasets, trained model binaries, evaluation metrics, and configuration files. The team needs to efficiently track these diverse artifacts, compare the performance metrics (e.g., precision, recall, F1-score) from each run, and easily identify the specific input datasets and hyperparameters that led to the best-performing models, to ultimately promote the optimal model to production. Manual tracking has become unsustainable and error-prone. What should you do?
questions.key: Utilize Vertex AI Experiments to associate each pipeline run with an experiment, then use its interface to compare the parameters, metrics, and output artifacts of all runs to identify the best model.

questions.stem: A distributed product team is developing a new Python-based machine learning model for a critical business application. The team consists of several data scientists who need to collaboratively work on Jupyter notebooks in real time, rapidly iterating on code and experiments. The solution must integrate seamlessly with existing Google Cloud resources for data and model training. Additionally, it is crucial to easily share the development notebooks with non-technical product managers and business stakeholders for review and feedback, leveraging existing Google Workspace identities without requiring complex environment setups or exports. The team also needs integrated version control to track changes and revert if necessary. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Colab Enterprise as the primary development environment, integrating notebooks with a Git repository for version control.

questions.stem: A large retail company is developing a machine learning model for real-time personalized product recommendations. The model requires features from several disparate sources: user interaction history (streaming from BigQuery), product catalog attributes (daily batch updates from Cloud SQL), and embeddings of recently viewed item images (stored in Cloud Storage after being generated by a separate processing pipeline). The company needs to consolidate these features and provide them to the recommendation model with extremely low latency for real-time inference requests. The solution must also support continuous updates for user-specific features and daily updates for product attributes, while minimizing operational overhead for feature management and serving. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Feature Store, creating separate entity types for users and products. Use Dataflow to continuously ingest streaming user interaction data from BigQuery into the user entity type, and to perform daily batch ingests of product catalog attributes from Cloud SQL into the product entity type. For image embeddings, process them into a structured format like Avro or Parquet in Cloud Storage, then use Dataflow to ingest these embeddings into the relevant entity type in Vertex AI Feature Store. Configure Vertex AI Feature Store for online serving to provide low-latency feature retrieval for real-time inference.

questions.stem:
A data science team has successfully developed and trained a custom image classification model using TensorFlow on Vertex AI Custom Training jobs. The model artifacts are currently stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. The team now needs to establish a robust process to manage different versions of this custom model, ensuring traceability from training to deployment. They require that each trained model version is automatically registered, includes metadata about its training run, and is readily available for deployment to various endpoints (e.g., online prediction, batch prediction) while maintaining clear lineage. Cost efficiency and operational overhead are also critical considerations.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Create a Vertex AI Training Pipeline that encapsulates the custom training job and automatically uploads the resulting model artifacts to Vertex AI Model Registry.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company is developing a real-time product recommendation system that must generate personalized recommendations with high throughput and sub-100ms latency. The system needs to integrate complex user behavior patterns. The ML engineering team has extensive experience with Python and TensorFlow for building deep learning models and needs to train models on large datasets efficiently. They are open to leveraging advanced hardware if it significantly improves training time or model performance without excessive operational overhead. Cost-effectiveness is also a key consideration. What approach should the company take to build and train the recommendation model on Google Cloud?
questions.key: Implement a custom deep learning model using TensorFlow. Train the model using Vertex AI Custom Training with NVIDIA A100 GPUs and Vertex AI Hyperparameter Tuning for optimization.

questions.stem: A financial services company is developing a new fraud detection system on Google Cloud. Due to stringent regulatory requirements and internal audit policies, all model predictions must be fully explainable to demonstrate compliance and justify decisions. The data science team is proficient in various machine learning frameworks, including Scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, and PyTorch. The training data, consisting of millions of transactions with numerous features, is stored in Cloud Storage. The company needs to build a model that prioritizes interpretability, allowing auditors to understand the reasoning behind each fraud prediction. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI Custom Training with a containerized Scikit-learn or XGBoost model, explicitly designing the model architecture (e.g., Logistic Regression or Gradient Boosted Trees) to be inherently interpretable, and integrate logging of feature importances or rule sets from the model for audit purposes.

questions.stem: A large e-commerce company is migrating its existing, complex, multi-stage ML pipeline from an on-premises Kubernetes cluster to Google Cloud due to scalability and maintenance challenges. The pipeline consists of custom data preprocessing, distributed TensorFlow model training using custom code, and a custom post-processing step before model deployment. The team requires fine-grained control over each stage, expects to leverage their existing expertise with custom Python training applications, and needs a robust, automated, and repeatable end-to-end ML lifecycle solution. The solution must support specifying different machine types and accelerators for training. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement the multi-stage ML pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines, defining each stage as a custom component that executes a Vertex AI Custom Job with your custom TensorFlow training code and specifying the required machine types and accelerators.

questions.stem: A research team is developing a large image classification model, ResNet-1000, using Vertex AI Custom Training on an extensive dataset. Their current distributed TensorFlow training setup employs multiple NVIDIA A100 GPUs and is experiencing significant communication overhead and synchronization delays during gradient aggregation. This is leading to suboptimal scaling efficiency and extended training times, directly impacting computational cost. The team needs to resolve these communication bottlenecks to boost training throughput and reduce expenses while maintaining their existing TensorFlow GPU codebase. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure the Vertex AI Custom Training job to use machine types that support GPUDirect-RDMA, such as a3-ultragpu-8g or a4-highgpu-8g, to enhance inter-GPU communication speed and reduce gradient aggregation overhead.

questions.stem: A financial institution is developing a credit risk assessment model on Google Cloud. Due to stringent regulatory requirements and internal audit policies, they must maintain a complete and auditable lineage of every deployed model. This lineage must precisely trace which version of the raw dataset was used, all intermediate data transformations (preprocessing steps), and the exact model artifact that resulted from a specific training run. The solution needs to automate this tracking to minimize manual overhead and ensure consistency. The institution currently uses Vertex AI Pipelines for their ML workflows. What should you do to meet these auditability requirements?
questions.key: Implement the ML pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines, ensuring that each step produces and consumes artifacts, and rely on Vertex ML Metadata to automatically capture and track the lineage of datasets, preprocessing outputs, and model artifacts throughout the pipeline.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs to develop a new fraud detection model. The training data resides in two on-premises sources: a large Hadoop distributed file system (HDFS) containing historical transaction logs (in Parquet format) and a PostgreSQL database storing recent customer activity. The combined dataset for training is several petabytes. You need to efficiently integrate this data into a Vertex AI custom training job without manual data dumps, ensuring the entire process is automated, scalable, and repeatable for weekly model retraining. The model will be trained using a custom Python application. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Storage Transfer Service to move Hadoop data to Cloud Storage. Use Cloud Data Fusion to build an ETL pipeline for extracting data from PostgreSQL, transforming it, and loading it into BigQuery. In BigQuery, combine and prepare the datasets. Then, create a Vertex AI Pipeline to orchestrate a custom training job that reads the prepared data directly from BigQuery using a custom Python training application.

questions.stem: A financial institution has deployed a critical credit scoring model on Vertex AI to provide real-time loan approval decisions. The model processes sensitive customer data and is exposed to potential adversarial inputs that could subtly manipulate its predictions, leading to incorrect credit assessments or financial losses. The institution needs a proactive mechanism to identify when the model's input data or prediction outcomes deviate significantly, indicating potential exploitation, without requiring constant manual review. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Model Monitoring to continuously track data drift and prediction drift for the deployed credit scoring model and configure alerts for significant deviations.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company needs to migrate its existing complex, multi-stage ML pipeline from an on-premises Kubernetes cluster to Google Cloud. The pipeline consists of distinct steps: data preprocessing, custom model training using a proprietary algorithm, and model evaluation. The company requires a solution that provides robust orchestration for these stages, ensures reproducibility of the entire workflow, and can scale dynamically to handle increasing data volumes and model complexity. The solution must also integrate seamlessly with other Google Cloud services for data storage and model deployment. What should you do to meet these requirements efficiently?
questions.key: Implement the multi-stage ML pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines, defining each stage (data preprocessing, custom training, model evaluation) as a separate component that orchestrates Vertex AI Custom Jobs.

questions.stem: A machine learning engineering team is developing a massive deep learning model for real-time fraud detection, requiring efficient and scalable training. They are currently using Vertex AI Custom Training with a distributed TensorFlow setup across multiple GPU-enabled virtual machines. The current configuration utilizes n1-standard-64 machine types with eight NVIDIA_TESLA_V100 GPUs per machine. However, the team observes significant communication overhead between GPUs, leading to suboptimal training performance and underutilized compute resources. They need to drastically improve inter-GPU data transfer speed to accelerate training without rewriting their existing TensorFlow distributed training code significantly. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure the Vertex AI Custom Training job to use machine types like a3-ultragpu-8g or a4-highgpu-8g which are equipped with GPUDirect-RDMA, and specify the corresponding acceleratorType and acceleratorCount.

questions.stem:
A financial institution has successfully deployed a new machine learning model on Vertex AI for fraud detection, replacing an older, simpler rule-based system. The new model processes real-time transaction data via a Vertex AI Endpoint. The business team needs continuous assurance that the new ML model consistently outperforms the established accuracy and precision of the deprecated rule-based system. They require immediate notification if the new model's performance drops below the baseline of the old system's performance metrics to avoid increased financial risk.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Deploy the new ML model to a Vertex AI Endpoint. Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to collect and analyze the model's prediction performance metrics, such as accuracy and precision, in real time. Establish custom thresholds in Cloud Monitoring based on the historical performance metrics of the rule-based system and configure alerts to trigger when the ML model's performance falls below these defined baselines.

questions.stem: A small e-commerce company wants to develop a churn prediction model. They have a moderately sized tabular dataset (approximately 8 million rows) stored in BigQuery, containing customer demographics, purchase history, and website interaction data. The company has a junior data science team with limited ML engineering resources and needs to quickly iterate on model development and deployment. They require a solution that minimizes custom code development and operational overhead while providing robust model training capabilities for a classification task. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI AutoML Tabular to train the churn prediction model by creating a Vertex AI Dataset from the BigQuery table.

questions.stem:
You are prototyping a generative AI application inside a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench notebook. You want to test an open-source foundation model (such as Gemma) available in Model Garden. To streamline your experimentation workflow directly within the Python notebook, you need to programmatically inspect Model Garden's verified hardware configurations (including supported machine types and accelerators) and deploy the model to a managed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform endpoint.

Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Initialize the vertexai library, instantiate the model using vertexai.model_garden.OpenModel, query verified hardware specifications using list_deploy_options(), and deploy the model to an endpoint by calling deploy() with accept_eula=True.

questions.stem: A research team is developing a novel deep learning model for medical image analysis that requires a highly customized training loop and specific GPU-accelerated pre-processing steps. These steps are implemented as separate Python scripts, and the entire process needs to be orchestrated into a repeatable and auditable workflow. The model training itself is computationally intensive and benefits significantly from distributed training across multiple NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The team needs to ensure efficient resource utilization, reproducibility, and clear separation of concerns between pre-processing and model training. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a Vertex AI Training Pipeline that orchestrates two Custom Jobs: one for the GPU-accelerated pre-processing steps and another for the distributed deep learning model training, configuring both Custom Jobs with appropriate NVIDIA A100 GPU machine types and replica counts.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company is developing a new recommendation engine. The ML engineering team has implemented an end-to-end ML workflow using Vertex AI Pipelines to orchestrate data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For auditing purposes and to enable easy comparison of different pipeline runs, the company requires an automated solution to meticulously record all input datasets, model binaries, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameter configurations for each pipeline execution. This solution must also establish clear lineage for all generated artifacts. The team needs to efficiently track and analyze experiment results directly from the pipeline runs. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure the Vertex AI Pipeline to associate each pipeline run with a Vertex AI Experiment, leveraging Vertex ML Metadata for automatic tracking of input datasets, model binaries, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameters, ensuring lineage and enabling comparison of runs.

questions.stem: A content creation agency wants to develop a highly customized text summarization tool for their vast, proprietary article corpus stored in Cloud Storage. They need to leverage a pre-trained Large Language Model (LLM) to achieve high-quality, domain-specific summaries. The solution must provide ease of access to suitable foundation models, enable fine-tuning with custom Python code and advanced hyperparameter tuning, and ensure the entire training workflow is repeatable and easily managed without excessive infrastructure overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Model Garden to select a suitable LLM, then fine-tune it by creating a Vertex AI Custom Training job with your custom Python training application, orchestrating the process with a Vertex AI Training Pipeline, and storing your proprietary data in Cloud Storage. Implement Vertex AI Hyperparameter Tuning within the pipeline for optimal model performance.

questions.stem: A data science team has developed a complex, multi-stage ML model for fraud detection. Their current prototype workflow involves custom Python scripts for data preprocessing, training a custom TensorFlow model, and a separate evaluation step that calculates custom metrics. They need to productionize this workflow on Google Cloud to ensure it is automated, repeatable, and scalable. The team requires full control over their custom code and wants to integrate the entire process, from data ingestion to model registration, into a single, orchestrated workflow. What should you do to meet these requirements efficiently?
questions.key: Implement the workflow using Vertex AI Pipelines, defining each stage as a custom component that executes the Python scripts and TensorFlow training on Vertex AI Custom Training.

questions.stem:
A government agency has deployed a critical Vertex AI model for allocating public resources. Due to strict regulatory requirements, the agency must ensure continuous fairness, explainability, and auditability for every prediction made by the model. This means not only detecting potential bias or performance degradation but also being able to explain why any specific resource allocation decision was made and to provide a detailed, immutable record of the decision process. The solution must integrate seamlessly with existing Google Cloud operations and minimize additional operational overhead.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a Vertex AI Endpoint with Vertex AI Explainable AI enabled, configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring for continuous detection of data and prediction drift, and stream prediction request and response logs, including explanation outputs, to Cloud Logging for auditability.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs to develop a highly accurate credit risk model using a large tabular dataset of 50 million rows and 200 features, currently stored in BigQuery. The data science team has limited ML engineering expertise and requires an approach that is opinionated and low-code, yet offers more customization and control than AutoML. Specifically, they need to implement custom Python-based feature engineering steps, including complex aggregations and transformations, before the model training begins. The final solution must be automated, repeatable, and able to handle the large dataset efficiently. What should you do?
questions.key: Develop a Vertex AI Pipeline using the Vertex AI SDK for Python, incorporating custom components for the required Python-based feature engineering steps, followed by a custom training job component to train the model, and finally, upload the trained model to Vertex AI Model Registry.

questions.stem: A research team is developing a novel large language model (LLM) using a custom TensorFlow architecture on Google Cloud. Their model is characterized by extremely large batch sizes, often exceeding 10,000, and its training process is heavily dominated by matrix multiplication operations. The team needs to significantly minimize the overall training time to accelerate research cycles and optimize the computational cost associated with these extensive training runs. They plan to use Vertex AI Custom Training for their workflow. What is the most efficient hardware configuration for this specific workload on Vertex AI?
questions.key: Configure a Vertex AI Custom Training job to use Cloud TPU v5e with a ct5lp-hightpu-8t machine type and an appropriate tpuTopology for large-scale training.

questions.stem: A financial institution has deployed a credit scoring model on Vertex AI. Recently, there have been concerns about potential data poisoning attempts affecting the model's predictions, leading to manipulated credit scores for certain applicants. The institution needs to continuously monitor the input data distribution for the online prediction endpoint to detect any significant deviations or anomalies that could indicate such attacks, while minimizing operational overhead. The solution must proactively identify shifts in the input data characteristics compared to the training data. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to monitor the online prediction endpoint, setting up data drift detection against the training dataset as a baseline and enabling alerting for significant deviations in input features.

questions.stem:
Your organization is selecting an open foundation model from Model Garden on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for a core customer-facing application. Your architecture must satisfy the following technical and compliance requirements:
Data regulations prohibit the use of multi-tenant managed services; the model serving infrastructure must reside entirely within your Google Cloud project and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network.
The application will experience steady, predictable, and continuous high-volume inference traffic where you need to optimize total cost of ownership (TCO).
Your team does not require custom preprocessing or postprocessing logic and wants to avoid the operational burden of building and maintaining custom container images.

Which model selection and serving strategy should you implement?
questions.key: Self-deploy an open model from Model Garden to a dedicated endpoint using an optimized prebuilt container image such as vLLM.

questions.stem: A machine learning engineering team is training a massive image classification model (ResNet-1000) using a custom training job on Vertex AI. They are currently utilizing a2-ultragpu-8g machine types, each configured with eight NVIDIA_TESLA_A100 GPUs for distributed training. Despite scaling the number of GPUs, they observe significant communication overhead during gradient synchronization, leading to suboptimal scaling efficiency and longer training times. The team needs to reduce inter-GPU communication latency and improve throughput to accelerate training without rewriting their distributed training framework. What should you do?
questions.key: Migrate the custom training job on Vertex AI to a machine type with GPUDirect-RDMA capabilities, such as a3-ultragpu-8g with NVIDIA_H200_141GB GPUs.

questions.stem:
A government agency has deployed a critical machine learning model on Vertex AI Prediction for real-time resource allocation. The model processes sensitive public data, and the agency has a strict requirement to continuously monitor and protect it from adversarial attacks or data manipulation attempts that could lead to biased or incorrect allocations. Any potential exploitation or anomalous input patterns must be detected immediately to prevent misuse and maintain public trust. The agency needs a solution that provides real-time alerts for suspicious activities without significant manual overhead.

What should you do to continuously monitor and protect the model?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Model Monitoring on the deployed endpoint to detect data drift, specifically monitoring the distribution of input features, and configure custom alerts in Cloud Monitoring to notify security teams of significant deviations.

questions.stem: A financial institution is developing a new deep learning model on Google Cloud for real-time fraud detection. The model processes a very large, sparse tabular dataset containing billions of records, with the architecture heavily relying on numerous embedding layers followed by dense neural network layers. The team needs to train this model efficiently, minimizing training time while handling the large dataset and complex model structure. They require full control over the training pipeline and the underlying hardware to optimize performance. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure a Vertex AI Custom Training job with a single worker pool specifying a Cloud TPU v5e or v6e machine type (e.g., ct5lp-hightpu-4t with an appropriate tpuTopology) set to replicaCount=1 for distributed training across multiple TPU chips.

questions.stem: A machine learning engineering team is developing a large-scale image classification model using TensorFlow on Vertex AI. They are currently training on a multi-GPU setup, but are experiencing significant communication bottlenecks between GPUs, leading to extended training times and underutilization of resources. The model's complexity requires substantial inter-GPU data transfer. The team needs to scale their training efficiently, mitigate these communication bottlenecks, and minimize changes to their existing multi-GPU TensorFlow training code. What should you do to optimize the training infrastructure?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Custom Training to use a3-ultragpu-8g machine types with 8 NVIDIA_H200_141GB GPUs, leveraging GPUDirect-RDMA features for enhanced inter-GPU communication.

questions.stem: A healthcare organization is developing a new AI model on Vertex AI for early diagnosis of a critical condition. This model will interact directly with patient data, and its predictions must be rigorously fair and unbiased across diverse demographic groups (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity) to ensure ethical and compliant patient care. Before deploying the model for wider use, the MLOps team needs to systematically assess the model's fairness and identify any potential biases in its predictions. The solution must provide a structured and repeatable way to evaluate these aspects during the development phase. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI Model Evaluation during the development phase to run evaluations, including subgroup analysis and counterfactual generation, to identify and mitigate potential biases across demographic groups.

questions.stem: A financial institution is developing a fraud detection model using a highly complex XGBoost algorithm. The model needs to be trained on a very large tabular dataset consisting of hundreds of millions of rows and thousands of features. The training process requires significant computational power and memory to handle the dataset efficiently and complete within a reasonable timeframe. The team wants to use Vertex AI Custom Training for this task and is looking for the most efficient and cost-effective compute configuration. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure a Vertex AI Custom Training job to use multiple n2-highmem machine types in a distributed setup, without accelerators.

questions.stem: A financial institution is developing a large, dense neural network for real-time fraud detection. The model is trained using Vertex AI Custom Training with multiple NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Due to the model's architecture and a fixed, large batch size, the team observes significant communication overhead between workers during distributed training, leading to a communication bottleneck that limits scalability and increases training times. The current A100 GPUs do not fully mitigate this inter-GPU communication issue. The team needs to optimize the training infrastructure to reduce communication latency and improve overall training efficiency for their large-scale distributed workload. What should you do?
questions.key: Migrate the Vertex AI Custom Training job to use machine types equipped with NVIDIA H100 GPUs, specifically leveraging their GPUDirect Networking capabilities, and configure the WorkerPoolSpec with the appropriate machineType and acceleratorType.

questions.stem: A retail company has deployed a real-time recommendation engine using a custom model on a Vertex AI Endpoint to personalize customer experiences. Recently, users have reported intermittent service disruptions, characterized by 5xx errors and increased latency during peak hours. The model's accuracy and feature attribution metrics, as monitored by Vertex AI Model Monitoring, remain within acceptable thresholds. The MLOps team needs to quickly identify the root cause of these operational errors to restore stable service without altering the model's core logic. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Cloud Monitoring to track request rate, error rate, and latency for the Vertex AI Endpoint, and then use Cloud Logging to analyze detailed logs for the identified 5xx errors to pinpoint specific failure reasons.

questions.stem:
You are building an interactive web application that allows users to upload technical product manuals in native PDF format and immediately download translated Spanish versions. Each native PDF manual is approximately 120 pages (15 MB in size). The translated manuals must preserve the original document layout, font styles, and hyperlinks, and must enforce company-approved technical terminology using a predefined glossary. 

How should you design the translation pipeline to meet these requirements with minimal operational overhead?
questions.key: Send a synchronous request using the Cloud Translation - Advanced translateDocument method, providing the glossary configuration, specifying the source language code, and setting isTranslateNativePdfOnly to true.

questions.stem:
A bioinformatics research team is developing a novel transformer-based model on Google Cloud for analyzing large-scale genomic data. This model incorporates a highly irregular sparse attention mechanism and utilizes several custom TensorFlow operations not natively optimized for all accelerator architectures. The team's experiments show that the model's performance heavily relies on frequent, small matrix multiplications and benefits significantly from highly flexible programming to implement its unique computational patterns. They need to train this model on Vertex AI, prioritizing computational efficiency and the ability to finely tune custom operations, while also managing costs for potentially long training runs.

Which Google Cloud accelerator configuration should the team choose for their Vertex AI Custom Training job? What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Custom Training to use NVIDIA A100 GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA_TESLA_A100 or NVIDIA_A100_80GB) on a compatible machine type.

questions.stem: A global IoT company is developing a machine learning model for real-time anomaly detection on sensor data collected from industrial machinery. The model is a complex neural network that requires substantial computational resources for training. However, the final model must be deployed for inference directly on edge devices with severely limited power, memory, and computational resources, requiring very low latency. The training pipeline must be robust, cost-effective, and leverage Google Cloud Vertex AI. The company needs to ensure that the model trained in the cloud is optimized for efficient performance on these constrained edge devices. What should you do to configure the Vertex AI training pipeline to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Implement the training pipeline using Vertex AI Custom Training with lightweight neural network architectures and model optimization techniques (e.g., quantization-aware training, pruning) in your custom code. Configure the Custom Job to run on g2-standard machine types with NVIDIA L4 GPUs for efficient training.

questions.stem: A financial services company is developing a new fraud detection model that needs to be deployed for online inference to internal applications. The model will receive sensitive customer transaction data and must meet stringent security and compliance requirements, ensuring all inference traffic remains within Google Cloud's private network. The company plans to frequently iterate on the model, requiring the ability to deploy new versions and conduct A/B testing with traffic splitting to compare performance before full rollout. Latency for predictions must be optimized, and the solution should support payload sizes up to 5 MB with request timeouts up to 5 minutes. The ML Engineering team wants to leverage a fully managed service to minimize operational overhead for ML inference. What should you do to deploy and manage this model?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect on Vertex AI.

questions.stem:
A financial services company uses a machine learning model on Google Cloud to predict customer churn in real-time, requiring low-latency online predictions. The MLOps team needs to regularly deploy new iterations of this model for A/B testing against the current production model, observe their performance, and quickly roll back to a previous stable version if a new model performs poorly. All model versions must be securely stored and easily retrievable. The solution must support these requirements with minimal operational overhead and ensure efficient resource utilization.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Store all model iterations in Vertex AI Model Registry. Deploy the current production model and the new candidate model to a single Vertex AI public endpoint, configuring traffic splitting to direct a small percentage of incoming requests to the new model for A/B testing. Adjust traffic split percentages for rollback or full rollout.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company needs to re-score petabytes of historical customer interaction data to update product recommendations using a newly trained PyTorch model. This requires extensive pre-processing, including joining data from various internal and external sources (e.g., transactional databases, web logs, third-party demographic data), complex feature engineering, and data cleaning before the model generates predictions. The re-scored data must be efficiently stored in BigQuery for subsequent analysis. The company seeks a cost-effective, scalable, and fully managed batch prediction pipeline. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a Dataflow pipeline to read data from various sources, perform the complex pre-processing and feature engineering, integrate the PyTorch model for batch predictions, and write the results to BigQuery.

questions.stem: A small startup is developing a public-facing customer support portal that requires real-time classification of incoming support tickets. They have trained a scikit-learn model for this purpose and anticipate moderate traffic, around several hundred inference requests per minute, with a need for low-latency responses. The team prioritizes cost-efficiency, minimal operational overhead, and secure, reliable data flow. They specifically lack expertise in building and managing custom Docker containers for model serving. What should you do to deploy this model for online inference?
questions.key: Deploy the scikit-learn model to a Vertex AI Endpoint using a dedicated public endpoint and a pre-built scikit-learn container.

questions.stem: A financial institution has developed a new PyTorch model for real-time fraud detection and needs to deploy it on Google Cloud. The model will receive prediction requests from both on-premises systems and applications running in a Google Cloud VPC, requiring strictly private network communication without any public internet exposure. The solution must support prediction request payloads up to 10 MB, provide optimized network latency, and allow for A/B testing of future model versions. Additionally, the system needs to handle a very high volume of queries per minute (QPM). What should you do to deploy this model?
questions.key: Deploy the PyTorch model to a Vertex AI dedicated private endpoint configured with Private Service Connect.

questions.stem: An autonomous driving company is using Vertex AI for its machine learning operations. They currently have model_v1.0 deployed and serving online inferences to vehicles through a secure, low-latency connection within their Google Cloud VPC. A new model_v1.1 has been developed, demonstrating improved object detection accuracy. The MLOps team needs to register model_v1.1 in Vertex AI Model Registry, ensure its performance metrics are documented, and prepare it for an eventual staged rollout (A/B testing) to a small percentage of vehicles before full promotion. During this process, model_v1.0 must remain available for immediate rollback. The solution must maintain the existing secure, low-latency private network communication from the vehicles to the inference service. What should you do?
questions.key: Upload model_v1.1 to Vertex AI Model Registry. Create a new Vertex AI private endpoint for model_v1.1 and deploy model_v1.1 to it. Configure the vehicle client applications to manually split a small percentage of inference requests to model_v1.1's private endpoint, while the majority continue to model_v1.0's existing private endpoint.

questions.stem: A large healthcare organization is developing a diagnostic AI model on Google Cloud. This model will be used in clinical settings, making it critical to ensure the model adheres to strict fairness and ethical standards before deployment. The organization must proactively assess the model's readiness, specifically identifying and mitigating potential biases related to sensitive patient attributes, to align with Google's Responsible AI practices. The solution needs to provide a robust pre-deployment evaluation process that can detect subtle biases and ensure equitable performance across different patient groups. What should you do?
questions.key: Utilize Vertex AI Model Evaluation during the development phase to perform subgroup analysis on sensitive patient attributes, define custom evaluation metrics for fairness, and integrate human-in-the-loop workflows to assess generated outputs against ethical guidelines before deploying the model to a Vertex AI endpoint.

questions.stem: A global media company needs to deploy two distinct machine learning models for online inference. Model A is a large language model optimized for CPU inference, requiring high throughput and extremely low latency for real-time content generation. Model B is a computer vision model that is heavily GPU-bound, also requiring high throughput and low latency for real-time image analysis. Both models must be accessible from the company's on-premises data centers via a private network connection, with absolutely no exposure to the public internet for security and compliance reasons. The solution must also be cost-efficient by precisely matching hardware to model requirements and be highly maintainable. What should you do to deploy these models to meet all requirements?
questions.key: Upload both models to Vertex AI Model Registry. Create two distinct Vertex AI Endpoints, each configured as a dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect. Deploy Model A to one endpoint with a CPU-optimized machine type, and Model B to the other with a GPU-accelerated machine type. Establish private connectivity from on-premises data centers to these Private Service Connect endpoints.

questions.stem: A global media company needs to deploy a large language model (LLM) for real-time content summarization. The model is computationally intensive and has been optimized for inference on specialized hardware. The solution must achieve very low latency, specifically under 50 milliseconds, and handle fluctuating traffic patterns with peaks up to 10,000 queries per second (QPS). The company is sensitive to operational costs but prioritizes meeting the strict performance requirements. You need to select a serving strategy on Google Cloud that leverages Vertex AI. What should you do?
questions.key: Deploy the LLM to a Vertex AI Endpoint configured with GPU accelerators and enable autoscaling to handle traffic fluctuations.

questions.stem: A financial institution has deployed a critical fraud detection model on Vertex AI for real-time transaction analysis. Recently, the model's false negative rate for specific, complex transaction patterns has increased, leading to significant financial losses. The MLOps team suspects sophisticated adversarial attacks or data poisoning attempts are subtly manipulating model predictions, making it difficult to identify fraudulent transactions. The institution requires a solution to proactively detect this model degradation, understand the reasons for misclassifications, and maintain high detection accuracy. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Model Monitoring to track prediction drift and feature attribution drift, configure alerts for deviations in key metrics, and integrate Vertex AI Explainable AI (XAI) to analyze feature importances for transactions flagged as suspicious by domain experts or showing unusual behavior.

questions.stem: A retail company has developed a deep learning recommendation model for its online product recommendation service. The current model is 20 GB in size and exhibits an average inference latency of 200 ms when tested in a staging environment. The company needs to deploy this model for online serving on Google Cloud, requiring an average inference latency under 80 ms, reduced memory footprint for cost efficiency, and the ability to scale automatically with varying user traffic. The solution must prioritize minimal operational overhead while ensuring high availability. What should you do?
questions.key: Optimize the deep learning model through techniques such as quantization or pruning to reduce its size and improve inference speed. Then, upload the optimized model to Vertex AI Model Registry and deploy it to a dedicated public Vertex AI Endpoint, configuring autoscaling to handle traffic fluctuations.

questions.stem:
A FinTech startup is developing a real-time credit scoring application on Google Cloud. The application requires predictions with sub-100ms latency for online transactions, handling high request volumes. The credit scoring model relies on hundreds of features per user, which are pre-computed and frequently updated offline. These features must be consistently available for both model training and online inference. Due to strict financial regulations, all data access for inference must occur over a private network connection, and the solution must support seamless model updates without service interruption.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Store and serve the pre-computed features using Vertex AI Feature Store for online serving. Deploy the credit scoring model to a Vertex AI dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect to serve predictions over a private network.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company has deployed a new product recommendation model, developed on Vertex AI, into production. This new model replaced a simpler, rule-based recommendation system that served as the previous baseline. Business stakeholders require continuous verification that the new Vertex AI model consistently outperforms the old rule-based baseline. Additionally, they need to identify any performance degradation or dips over specific time periods to ensure sustained value. You need to set up a monitoring solution that can track the new model's performance relative to the baseline and detect temporal performance changes. What should you do?
questions.key: Deploy the new Vertex AI model to an endpoint and configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to track its performance. In Model Monitoring, define a custom metric for the new model's performance and continuously compare it against the performance of the historical rule-based system as a baseline. Use Cloud Monitoring to visualize these metrics over time and set up alerts for deviations.

questions.stem:
You are an ML engineer managing features for a real-time fraud detection model using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Store. You need to consolidate customer demographic features and historical transaction features stored in two separate BigQuery tables. The transaction table contains multiple historical records per customer entity. Your solution must register the features in the Feature Registry for team discovery and drift monitoring, and serve the latest feature values from both sources through a single low-latency online serving endpoint.

How should you configure the Feature Store architecture?
questions.key: Ensure the historical transaction table contains an entity ID column and a feature_timestamp column. Create a separate Feature Group for each BigQuery table, define Features under each Feature Group mapped to the corresponding columns, and create a Feature View in an online store instance that references both Feature Groups.

questions.stem:
Your organization stores hundreds of thousands of customer support transcripts and verified resolution responses in a BigQuery table located in us-central1. You need to fine-tune a Gemini foundation model using supervised tuning so that its generated responses adhere to your company's tone and resolution formatting. You want to execute the fine-tuning process directly within BigQuery using standard SQL without exporting the dataset to Cloud Storage or writing custom Python scripts. 

You have created a BigQuery Cloud resource connection in the same region. What should you do next to perform the supervised fine-tuning?
questions.key: Grant the Vertex AI Service Agent role to the Cloud resource connection's service account, and run a CREATE MODEL statement using the REMOTE WITH CONNECTION clause with the Gemini endpoint specified in OPTIONS and training data supplied via the AS SELECT clause.

questions.stem: A financial services company is developing a fraud detection system that requires real-time predictions with extremely low latency (under 100ms) and highly secure access to sensitive customer data. The system needs to ingest and serve frequently updated features (e.g., transaction velocity, account balance changes) from Vertex AI Feature Store. The predictive model, trained on tabular data, will be deployed on Vertex AI. The company mandates that all prediction traffic must remain entirely within Google Cloud's private network and be compatible with VPC Service Controls for enhanced data exfiltration prevention.
