Future requirements include the ability to perform A/B testing of new model versions without downtime. What should you do to deploy the model for online serving?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect on Vertex AI, ensuring the endpoint is configured within a VPC that can securely access Vertex AI Feature Store.

questions.stem: A financial institution has deployed a large, complex deep learning model on Vertex AI for real-time fraud detection. The model receives a high volume of inference requests (thousands of QPS) from an on-premises data center and requires sub-100ms end-to-end latency, along with strict network security for all communications. Despite provisioning powerful machine types for the Vertex AI Endpoint, monitoring shows that the model's internal processing time is the primary bottleneck, causing latency spikes above the 100ms threshold under peak load. The institution also needs to ensure private network connectivity for compliance. What should you do to meet the latency and security requirements?
questions.key: Apply model optimization techniques to reduce the model's size and complexity, then deploy the optimized model to a Vertex AI dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect.

questions.stem:
A financial services institution uses a machine learning model deployed on Vertex AI for automated credit risk assessment. Due to regulatory requirements and internal Responsible AI policies, the institution must provide clear, interpretable reasons for each credit decision. Additionally, they need to proactively identify potential hidden biases or vulnerabilities within the model's decision-making process to ensure fairness and prevent unintentional exploitation. The solution must be scalable and integrated with their existing Google Cloud ML ecosystem.

What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Explainable AI to generate feature attributions for each prediction and analyze these attributions to justify decisions and identify potential biases.

questions.stem: A leading research institution has developed a massive, computationally intensive deep learning model for real-time image analysis. This model requires extremely high throughput and ultra-low latency for online inference, processing thousands of requests per second with sub-100ms response times. The institution needs to deploy this model as a managed service on Google Cloud, ensuring secure access from its internal VPC network without exposing the endpoint to the public internet. The model's architecture is specifically optimized to take advantage of parallel processing capabilities found in specialized AI accelerators. What should you do to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a Vertex AI Endpoint, configuring the deployed model with a machine type that includes Cloud TPUs and utilizing a dedicated private endpoint.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs to deploy a real-time credit risk prediction model for online inference. The model requires several precomputed features that are updated hourly and must be available with extremely low latency. The system is expected to handle thousands of queries per second (QPS) with an end-to-end prediction latency requirement of under 100 milliseconds. All inference traffic must remain within a private network due to strict security and compliance regulations, and the solution must support production enterprise applications. What should you do to deploy this model and ensure its features are served efficiently?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a Vertex AI dedicated private endpoint using Private Service Connect and retrieve precomputed features from Vertex AI Feature Store.

questions.stem: A medical imaging startup has developed a large deep learning model (50 GB) for real-time disease diagnosis from high-resolution images. They need to deploy this model for online inference, expecting moderate but burstable traffic, with a strict requirement for inference latency under 200 ms. The solution must be cost-effective and allow for traffic splitting to facilitate A/B testing of future model versions. Direct access from client applications over the public internet is required for ease of integration with partner systems. What should you do?
questions.key: Deploy the model to a Vertex AI dedicated public endpoint, specifying GPU machine types for the deployed model, and configure autoscaling to handle burstable traffic.

questions.stem:
Your team is building a machine learning solution in BigQuery to forecast retail product demand across multiple store locations. The data includes historical sales as well as external factors such as planned promotional markdowns. Business stakeholders require the ability to understand individual future forecast values, specifically decomposing how baseline trend, seasonality, holidays, and each external promotional factor contributed to the prediction.

Which model type and BigQuery ML function should you use to fulfill these interpretability requirements?
questions.key: Train an ARIMA_PLUS_XREG model and inspect individual forecast attributions using the ML.EXPLAIN_FORECAST function.

questions.stem: An international e-commerce company plans to deploy a real-time product recommendation engine. The model, hosted on Vertex AI, needs to serve predictions to a global user base with extremely low latency and high availability. The solution must be resilient to regional outages and capable of automatically scaling to handle unpredictable traffic spikes. The company requires a secure and reliable setup for production. You have deployed the model to Vertex AI Endpoints in us-central1 and europe-west1. What should you do to ensure optimal performance, high availability, and global distribution for inference requests?
questions.key: Deploy the model to Vertex AI dedicated public endpoints in each region and configure a Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancer with the regional Vertex AI endpoints as backends.

questions.stem: A large enterprise is developing a machine learning (ML) solution to predict product demand. The solution requires processing historical sales data from an on-premises data warehouse, transforming it using a scalable data processing service, training a custom model on a managed ML platform, and then publishing the prediction results to an external business intelligence dashboard hosted outside Google Cloud. The entire workflow must run daily at a scheduled time, handle complex interdependencies between data extraction, processing, training, and reporting, and maintain lineage for all artifacts. The team needs a robust, managed orchestration service that can seamlessly integrate with both Google Cloud services and external systems. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement the end-to-end ML pipeline using Cloud Composer to orchestrate tasks including an on-premises data extraction, a Dataflow job for data transformation, a Vertex AI Pipelines job for model training and deployment, and a custom task to push results to the external dashboard.

questions.stem: A retail company is implementing an MLOps strategy on Google Cloud for its product recommendation engine. New product data, arriving daily as CSV files in a Cloud Storage bucket, must undergo a quick, stateless schema and data quality validation before triggering the main model retraining pipeline. The validation process is lightweight, intermittent, and needs to be highly cost-effective, scaling to zero when inactive, and reacting immediately to new file uploads. The existing model retraining workflow is already defined as a Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) template, managed in Artifact Registry, and needs to be executed on Vertex AI Pipelines upon successful validation. What should you do to automate this validation and pipeline triggering process?
questions.key: Implement a Cloud Function triggered by Cloud Storage object finalization events, which performs the data validation and, upon success, uses the Vertex AI SDK for Python to submit a new run of the Vertex AI Pipeline template.

questions.stem:
A pharmaceutical company is developing multiple machine learning models for drug discovery. These models require strict auditability and reproducibility to meet regulatory compliance standards. The MLOps team needs to establish an end-to-end pipeline that ensures every trained model can be traced back to the exact version of the raw dataset, the specific preprocessing steps applied, and the training code used. Furthermore, all model versions must be managed and easily retrievable. The solution must be scalable, minimize operational overhead, and provide clear lineage.

What should you do to meet these requirements on Google Cloud?
questions.key: Develop the ML pipelines using the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK within Vertex AI Pipelines, store raw and processed datasets in versioned Cloud Storage buckets, manage pipeline component container images in Artifact Registry, and register all trained models in Vertex AI Model Registry.

questions.stem: A data science team is developing a new ML pipeline on Google Cloud for a critical real-time inference model. The pipeline needs to handle three distinct stages: first, a heavy batch data transformation process on terabytes of structured data; second, a lightweight, stateless model evaluation step that runs frequently; and third, a custom containerized model training job requiring specific GPU configurations. The solution must be cost-optimized, ensure efficient resource utilization for each stage, and allow dynamic adjustment of training hyperparameters based on external triggers, such as new data availability. The team needs to orchestrate this end-to-end workflow to ensure repeatability and maintainability. What should you do?
questions.key: Design the pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK. Implement the data transformation stage using Dataflow, the model evaluation stage as a lightweight component running on Cloud Run, and the custom training stage as a custom training job on Vertex AI. Parameterize the pipeline to accept hyperparameters, and use the Vertex AI SDK for Python to submit pipeline runs, dynamically passing parameters based on Pub/Sub messages.

questions.stem:
A financial institution is developing a new fraud detection system on Google Cloud. The system requires an end-to-end ML pipeline that can handle large volumes of transactional data, ensure robust data validation at every stage, and guarantee consistent feature engineering between training and serving. The institution has a strict requirement for high reliability and auditability, necessitating schema enforcement and the ability to detect data drift promptly. The MLOps team prefers to define pipelines using Kubeflow DSL for reusability and version control.

What should you do to build this ML pipeline, ensuring strict data validation and consistent preprocessing?
questions.key: Develop the ML pipeline using the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK to define components for Vertex AI Pipelines, incorporating TFX components such as ExampleGen, StatisticsGen, SchemaGen, ExampleValidator, and Transform for data ingestion, validation, and feature engineering.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company relies on a recommendation engine model, retrained weekly by a Vertex AI Pipeline, to personalize user experiences. Recently, after a scheduled model update, customer engagement metrics plummeted, indicating a significant regression. The MLOps team needs to quickly debug this issue by tracing the lineage of the problematic model, identifying the specific dataset version and pipeline run that introduced the regression, and comparing its evaluation metrics against previous successful versions to enable a rapid rollback. What is the most efficient solution for the MLOps team to debug this issue and facilitate a rapid rollback?
questions.key: Leverage Vertex AI Pipelines to review the execution history, use Vertex AI Experiments to compare the performance metrics and parameters of the problematic pipeline run with previous successful runs, and utilize Vertex AI Model Registry to inspect the deployed model version and facilitate a rollback to a stable prior version.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs to develop an automated fraud detection system. The system requires daily training of a TensorFlow model using sensitive transaction data. Due to strict compliance regulations, raw transaction data must first be processed and anonymized on-premises by a legacy system before being uploaded to a Google Cloud Storage bucket. Once the anonymized data is available in Cloud Storage, a machine learning pipeline must automatically pick it up, train a new TensorFlow model using Vertex AI, and then deploy the updated model to a Vertex AI Endpoint. The entire end-to-end process, including the trigger for the on-premises data processing and the subsequent cloud-based ML workflow, needs to be fully orchestrated, scheduled daily, and monitored from Google Cloud. What should you do to design this end-to-end ML pipeline?
questions.key: Implement a workflow using Cloud Composer. Within the Cloud Composer DAG, define a task to trigger the on-premises data processing system. Once the on-premises process uploads the anonymized data to Cloud Storage, define a subsequent task in the same DAG that uses the Vertex AI SDK for Python to submit a Vertex AI Pipeline job for training and deploying the TensorFlow model. Schedule the Cloud Composer DAG to run daily.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company is developing a recommendation engine using TensorFlow Extended (TFX) on Vertex AI Pipelines. Their current pipeline includes ExampleGen for data ingestion and Trainer for model training. They observe degraded model performance in production due to feature skew and data drift between training and serving environments, and inconsistent feature transformations. The team needs to implement a robust solution to proactively detect data anomalies, validate schemas, and ensure consistent preprocessing. What additional TFX components should be integrated into their Vertex AI Pipeline to address these issues and maintain model quality? What should you do?
questions.key: Integrate StatisticsGen, SchemaGen, ExampleValidator, and Transform into the Vertex AI Pipeline. Connect ExampleGen output to StatisticsGen. Connect StatisticsGen output to SchemaGen (for training data) and ExampleValidator (for both training and serving data). Connect SchemaGen output to ExampleValidator. Finally, connect ExampleGen output, SchemaGen output, and StatisticsGen output to Transform, which then feeds its output to Trainer.

questions.stem: A media company uses a Vertex AI Pipeline, built with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK, to process user engagement data and train a personalized content recommendation model. A critical preprocessing step requires calling a custom, proprietary text embedding service to generate embeddings for new textual data. This embedding service is a lightweight Python microservice, completely stateless, and must scale independently based on the fluctuating volume of new data. The company needs a solution that is highly scalable, cost-effective (paying only for actual usage), and integrates seamlessly as a step within the existing Vertex AI Pipeline without introducing significant operational overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Develop the text embedding service as a Docker container, deploy it to Cloud Run, and create a custom Kubeflow Pipelines component within the Vertex AI Pipeline that invokes the Cloud Run service.

questions.stem: A financial institution uses a fraud detection model deployed on a Vertex AI Endpoint. The model's performance is critical, and it must be continuously updated to adapt to new fraud patterns. You need to implement an automated retraining policy where the model is retrained and redeployed only when its performance (F1-score) on a validation dataset drops below a predefined threshold, or when significant data drift is detected in the incoming transaction data. The new model must only replace the existing production model if its F1-score is demonstrably better. The solution must minimize operational overhead and ensure seamless integration with existing Vertex AI services. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement a Vertex AI Pipeline that includes steps for data ingestion, model training, evaluation, and conditional deployment. Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to detect F1-score degradation and data drift, and set up an alert that triggers the Vertex AI Pipeline to initiate a retraining run. Within the pipeline, include a component that evaluates the newly trained model against the current production model's F1-score and only proceeds to deploy the new model to the Vertex AI Endpoint if it outperforms the existing one.

questions.stem: A financial institution has deployed a credit approval machine learning model on Vertex AI Prediction. Recently, the MLOps team suspects data poisoning attempts or adversarial attacks are impacting specific loan applications, leading to incorrect approvals or rejections for certain demographic groups. This exploitation is causing both financial risk and potential reputational damage due to compliance concerns. The team needs a solution to continuously detect these types of attacks and anomalous model behavior in production with minimal operational overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement Vertex AI Model Monitoring to continuously detect data drift in input features and prediction drift in model outputs, and leverage AI Protection within Security Command Center to monitor for suspicious activities and anomalous model behavior affecting AI assets.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company relies on an existing Jenkins CI/CD system for its software deployments. They have recently implemented a new process where a machine learning model, responsible for product recommendations, is automatically retrained daily using a Vertex AI Pipeline. Upon successful retraining, the new model is registered in Vertex AI Model Registry. The company needs to automate the promotion of this newly registered model to a staging environment for A/B testing against the current production model. This promotion process must include fetching the model from the registry, deploying it as a new version to an existing Vertex AI Endpoint, and running integration tests to validate its performance before gradually shifting traffic. The solution must leverage the existing Jenkins infrastructure while adopting Google Cloud best practices for ML CI/CD. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Jenkins to trigger a Cloud Build pipeline that fetches the latest model from Vertex AI Model Registry, deploys it to the existing Vertex AI Endpoint as a new model version with a small traffic split for A/B testing, and then executes integration tests against the new model version on the endpoint.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company has successfully deployed a new product recommendation model on Vertex AI, replacing an older, simpler rule-based system. The business team needs to continuously verify that the new model consistently outperforms the historical performance of the deprecated rule-based system in terms of key metrics like conversion rate and click-through rate. Additionally, they require a solution to monitor the new model's performance trends over several months to detect any gradual degradation or shifts. The solution must be automated, provide proactive alerts, and allow for comparison against the established baseline. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring for the deployed recommendation model, setting up custom metrics to track conversion rate and click-through rate. Establish the historical performance data of the rule-based system as a baseline within Model Monitoring. Configure alerts for deviations from this baseline and for significant changes in the model's performance trends over time using Cloud Monitoring.

questions.stem:
A pharmaceutical company is developing highly sensitive drug discovery models on Google Cloud, requiring strict regulatory compliance and auditable lineage for all model versions. The MLOps team needs to ensure that when a deployed model exhibits unexpected behavior, they can quickly trace back the exact training data, hyperparameters, code version, and all intermediate artifacts used to create that specific model. The model retraining process must be fully automated, and all metadata must be automatically captured and accessible. The current CI/CD process uses Cloud Build.

What should you do to meet these requirements for automated retraining, comprehensive metadata capture, and auditable lineage?
questions.key: Implement the entire ML workflow as a Kubeflow Pipeline within Vertex AI Pipelines, ensuring that each component explicitly logs relevant metadata (dataset versions, hyperparameters, metrics) to Vertex AI Model Registry. Configure Cloud Build to trigger scheduled runs of this Vertex AI Pipeline for automated retraining and model registration.

questions.stem: A financial institution uses a fraud detection model deployed on Vertex AI Endpoints. The model's performance is critical, and it must be automatically retrained and re-deployed if its F1-score drops below 0.85 in production to maintain accuracy and minimize financial losses. The retraining process is defined as a Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) workflow managed by Vertex AI Pipelines. You need to design a robust, event-driven solution to automatically trigger this retraining pipeline when the F1-score degradation is detected, ensuring minimal operational overhead and traceability. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to track the F1-score of the deployed model, setting an alert threshold at 0.85. Integrate the Model Monitoring alert with Cloud Monitoring to publish a message to a Pub/Sub topic when the threshold is breached. Create a Cloud Function that subscribes to this Pub/Sub topic and, upon receiving a message, triggers a new run of the Vertex AI Pipeline for model retraining and re-deployment.

questions.stem:
Your team is developing a customer churn classification model using customer interaction data stored in BigQuery. The team decides to train and evaluate the model directly within BigQuery ML. Stakeholders have established the following technical and interpretability requirements:

 The model must use a tree-based ensemble architecture to capture non-linear relationships.
 The system must provide exact local feature attributions for individual customer predictions so customer service agents understand why a specific customer was flagged.
The system must provide global feature attributions aggregated across the evaluation dataset to satisfy auditing requirements.

Which model type and explainability configuration should you select in BigQuery ML?
questions.key: Train a Boosted Tree model, and use the Tree SHAP explainability method with ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT for local feature attributions and ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN for global feature attributions.

questions.stem: An e-commerce company uses an existing on-premises Jenkins setup to manage its software deployments. They have developed a new recommendation model, and the training and evaluation steps are orchestrated using a Vertex AI Pipeline. After a successful pipeline run that registers a new model version in Vertex AI Model Registry, the company needs to automatically deploy this new model version to a pre-existing Vertex AI Endpoint. This deployment must be initiated by their on-premises Jenkins, leveraging a custom Jenkins job. The solution must ensure secure access from Jenkins to Google Cloud and maintain the automated CI/CD flow, without migrating their core CI/CD system from Jenkins. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure the Jenkins job to authenticate with Google Cloud using a service account key, then use the Vertex AI SDK for Python within the Jenkins job to retrieve the newly registered model from Vertex AI Model Registry and deploy it to the Vertex AI Endpoint.

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical company is developing a machine learning pipeline for drug discovery, which involves processing sensitive experimental data, training predictive models, and evaluating their efficacy. The company needs to ensure full auditability and reproducibility of every model version. This includes meticulously tracking all dataset versions used for training, linking specific model artifacts to the exact pipeline run that produced them, and storing all evaluation metrics. The solution must allow data scientists to easily query the lineage of any deployed model, tracing back to its raw data, preprocessing steps, and training parameters, to meet strict regulatory compliance and scientific validation requirements. The company aims for a managed service approach to minimize operational overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement the ML pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines, leverage its automatic metadata tracking capabilities, and use Vertex AI Model Registry to manage model versions and their associated metadata.

questions.stem: Your government agency is developing a machine learning model on Vertex AI to assist in allocating social welfare benefits. Before this model can be deployed to production, it must adhere to strict fairness guidelines, ensuring equitable outcomes across various applicant demographics (e.g., age groups, income levels, geographic locations). Your team needs to proactively identify and mitigate potential biases in the model's predictions during the development phase to align with Google's Responsible AI practices and avoid unintentional discrimination. The solution must involve Google Cloud services and be implemented before the model serves live predictions. What should your team do to assess and address fairness and bias in the model?
questions.key: Use Vertex AI model evaluation to perform subgroup analysis across different demographic features during the model development phase, analyze the evaluation metrics for disparate impact, and refine the model iteratively.

questions.stem: A financial institution operates a critical fraud detection model on Google Cloud, deployed to a Vertex AI Endpoint. The model's performance is paramount, and it must be automatically retrained and redeployed if its F1-score drops below 0.85 to maintain accuracy. The data science team has already developed a robust training and deployment pipeline using the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK, which is compiled and stored in Artifact Registry. You need to design a solution that continuously monitors the model's F1-score, triggers the existing Vertex AI Pipeline for retraining and redeployment when the threshold is breached, and minimizes operational overhead. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Vertex AI Model Monitoring to track the F1-score of the deployed model, setting up an alert that publishes a message to a Pub/Sub topic when the F1-score falls below 0.85. Create a Cloud Function triggered by this Pub/Sub message, which then uses the Vertex AI SDK for Python to submit a new run of the pre-existing Vertex AI Pipeline for model retraining and redeployment.

questions.stem: A company has deployed a critical fraud detection model on a Vertex AI endpoint. Recently, users have reported intermittent high latency and occasional 5xx errors when requesting predictions from the model. The engineering team needs to quickly diagnose the root cause of these serving issues to restore optimal performance. The solution must provide detailed insights into the endpoint's health and underlying infrastructure without significantly increasing operational complexity. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Cloud Monitoring to track request rate, error rate, latency, and resource utilization for the Vertex AI endpoint, and analyze Cloud Logging for detailed error messages and request logs to identify the specific causes of the failures.

questions.stem:
An enterprise machine learning team is developing an internal service to extract metadata from complex regulatory filings into a proprietary, domain-specific JSON syntax. In the current prototype, the team uses prompt engineering with a base Gemini model, supplying detailed system instructions and 15 few-shot demonstration examples in each API call. In production, this design causes high per-query inference costs and high latency due to the large token context. Additionally, the model occasionally hallucinates invalid keys that violate the proprietary schema. The team has curated a high-quality, verified dataset of 2,500 historical documents paired with valid target JSON outputs.

Which approach should the team take to ensure strict adherence to the custom syntax while reducing inference latency and cost?
questions.key: Use supervised fine-tuning on the Gemini foundation model using the labeled dataset in Cloud Storage, and update the production application to query the tuned model with concise prompts that omit the few-shot examples.

questions.stem: Your company uses an ML classifier to shortlist job applicants for recruiter review. Its monitoring dashboard shows stable overall accuracy. Recruiters regularly audit a representative sample of both shortlisted and rejected applicants, recording qualification labels and linking self-reported demographic groups for fairness analysis. You want to detect unequal rates of missed qualified applicants while minimizing changes to the running screening service. What should you do?
questions.key: Measure false-negative rates by demographic group on audited applicants, compare groups with uncertainty estimates, and track disparities across recurring monitoring windows.

questions.stem:
Your organization is preparing to deploy a multi-turn customer support chatbot using Gemini on Google Cloud. You need to protect the system against prompt injection attacks and unintentional leaks of sensitive data. Before implementing active blocking in production, the security team requires an evaluation period using live user traffic to monitor violation rates and establish a baseline for false positives without disrupting user interactions or blocking any requests.

Which design strategy adheres to Google Cloud recommended best practices for Model Armor?
questions.key: Configure separate Model Armor templates for user prompts and model responses, set the enforcement type to Inspect only with Cloud Logging enabled, and sanitize each incoming message individually without concatenating conversation history.

questions.stem:
Your organization is selecting a deployment and serving strategy for an open foundation model available in Model Garden on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. The production workload has predictable, continuous high-volume traffic, and company compliance regulations strictly prohibit sending inference data through multi-tenant managed services. Additionally, your team wants to optimize throughput using the vLLM serving framework without taking on the operational overhead of building and maintaining custom container images. 

Which model deployment option should you select?
questions.key: Self-deploy the open model to a dedicated endpoint in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using a prebuilt vLLM container image.

questions.stem:
Your organization is developing an internal web portal that enables legal analysts to view translated versions of contract agreements in real time. 

You need to architect an automated solution with the following requirements:
 Each input document is a native (digitally created, non-scanned) PDF file of approximately 150 pages and 15 MB in size.
 The translation must be completed synchronously within an interactive request-response cycle.
 The output document must preserve the original formatting, visual layout, font styling, and embedded hyperlinks.
 The solution must use managed Google Cloud AI APIs and minimize operational overhead and custom reconstruction code.

What should you do?
questions.key: Send a synchronous request to the Cloud Translation - Advanced translateDocument method with the document configured in documentInputConfig and isTranslateNativePdfOnly set to true.

questions.stem: You are improving a retailer's replenishment planning after the recent deployment of a dashboard that reports daily sales. Analysts maintain daily units sold by product and store in BigQuery and prepare replenishment reports through SQL. Store managers still estimate upcoming demand manually, and different stores show different recurring weekly sales patterns. You want to forecast daily demand for each product at each store while minimizing changes to the analysts' SQL workflow. What should you do?
questions.key: Build BigQuery ML time-series forecasting models using daily sales histories for each product-store combination. Incorporate the resulting daily unit forecasts into the existing SQL replenishment reports.

questions.stem: You are evaluating compute and accelerator options (CPUs, GPUs, and Cloud TPUs) to train machine learning models on Google Cloud. Based on Google Cloud architectural guidelines and accelerator characteristics, which workload is most appropriate to train on Cloud TPUs?
questions.key: A large deep learning model dominated by dense matrix multiplications, configured with static tensor dimensions and large batch sizes, with no custom operations inside the primary training loop.

questions.stem:
You serve real-time online predictions using a dedicated endpoint in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You have registered a new version of your model and want to deploy it to the endpoint to replace the currently serving model version. Your deployment strategy must satisfy the following constraints:

 Reuse the backing compute resources already provisioned for the current model deployment.
 Gradually migrate incoming prediction traffic to the new model version in proportion to the number of ready-to-serve replicas.
Avoid downtime during the deployment process.

What should you do?
questions.key: Submit a deployModel request to the endpoint that includes the rolloutOptions field, setting previousDeployedModel to the ID of the currently deployed model and defining the replica surge and unavailability settings.

questions.stem: You need to help reviewers at a used-car marketplace explain disputed vehicle valuations. The marketplace recently deployed a boosted-tree model in BigQuery ML that estimates sale prices from vehicle attributes and sales history. Reviewers see each predicted price but cannot tell which inputs contributed to unusually high or low estimates. You want reviewers to understand individual valuations relative to a typical valuation while minimizing changes to the running model. What should you do?
questions.key: Generate local feature attributions for each disputed valuation using the deployed model, and show reviewers which inputs raise or lower its estimate relative to the baseline.

questions.stem:
You are deploying a trained model to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for online inference. The serving pipeline requires custom input feature normalization (preprocessing) and custom score formatting with business rules (postprocessing). You want to integrate these pre- and post-processing steps directly into the serving container while minimizing development overhead, specifically avoiding the need to author a Dockerfile from scratch or write an HTTP model server. In addition, you must be able to test and debug the serving container on your local machine before deploying it to an endpoint.

What should you do?
questions.key: Implement the preprocessing and postprocessing methods in a custom Predictor class using Custom Prediction Routines (CPR), build the container using LocalModel.build_cpr_model, and verify it locally with deploy_to_local_endpoint.

questions.stem: You are monitoring a retailer's product recommendation service running on Agent Platform. During promotions, request queues grow and response times rise, but the replica count changes little. The backend uses CPU-based autoscaling, and CPU utilization barely changes as request volume increases. Traffic falls substantially between promotions. You want to maintain responsive recommendations during traffic peaks while minimizing idle serving capacity. Which scaling approach should you use?
questions.key: Load-test the backend to measure sustainable request throughput per replica. Configure request-based autoscaling on Agent Platform using that result, then validate recommendation response times under representative promotional traffic.

questions.stem:
You have deployed a custom PyTorch image classification model to a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform online prediction endpoint with dedicated GPU accelerators and dedicated resources (minReplicaCount set to 2, maxReplicaCount set to 10). To manage scaling, your team explicitly configured an autoscaling metric spec targeting CPU utilization (aiplatform.googleapis.com/prediction/online/cpu/utilization) at 60%. 

During a traffic surge, inference latency increases significantly. Monitoring reveals that GPU accelerator duty cycle exceeds 90%, while CPU utilization remains below 30%, preventing the endpoint from scaling beyond the minimum replica count. You need to resolve this issue so that the endpoint scales automatically based on GPU load, without undeploying the model or creating a new endpoint. 

What should you do?
questions.key: Call the mutateDeployedModel method on the endpoint to update autoscalingMetricSpecs to target GPU accelerator duty cycle (aiplatform.googleapis.com/prediction/online/accelerator/duty_cycle), and include the updated path in updateMask.

questions.stem: You recently expanded your company's insurance claim-cost prediction service to more product lines. Its XGBoost models already run on Agent Platform endpoints, with a separately maintained custom serving image for each model. Each model uses standard XGBoost prediction logic. As the model fleet grows, rebuilding and patching these images takes more engineering time. You want to preserve prediction behavior while minimizing the work required to maintain serving images. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Export each XGBoost model for a compatible prebuilt prediction container, validate predictions against its current deployment, and deploy the resulting model to its existing Agent Platform endpoint.

questions.stem: You manage a retail demand forecasting pipeline that guides store replenishment. Its nightly workload is moving to Agent Platform Pipelines, and the current release step promotes a retrained model whenever the run succeeds. Supplier data occasionally changes, and successful runs have produced forecasts less accurate than the production model. Your team maintains a representative held-out dataset of historical sales. You want to prevent unreliable releases while minimizing manual review. What should you do?
questions.key: Add automated schema and distribution checks for each incoming batch. Release a candidate only after it meets predefined quality criteria when evaluated against the production model on the same representative held-out sales dataset.

questions.stem:
Your machine learning team maintains a domain-specific entity extraction and classification service. In production, the system sends lengthy prompts containing detailed syntax instructions and multiple few-shot examples to a foundation model. While task accuracy is acceptable, the team faces high per-call API token costs and high inference latency. The team has collected and validated 1,500 representative input-output pairs that match the expected production distribution.

Following Google Cloud best practices, how should you address the latency and cost challenges while maintaining extraction accuracy and minimizing training resource requirements?
questions.key: Perform parameter-efficient supervised fine-tuning (adapter tuning) on the foundation model using the labeled dataset, and remove the few-shot examples and lengthy instructions from production prompts.

questions.stem: You are maintaining an insurer's customer-churn training workflow in Agent Platform Pipelines. The pipeline has separate preprocessing, training, and evaluation components. During each development cycle, engineers run several model candidates against the same customer-data snapshot using unchanged, deterministic preprocessing. Each run repeats preprocessing, which accounts for most elapsed time and compute spending; training is comparatively short. You want to shorten repeated candidate runs while minimizing compute spending. What should you do?
questions.key: Enable preprocessing execution caching in Agent Platform Pipelines, represent data snapshots and transformation versions as component inputs, and reuse matching preprocessing outputs across candidate runs.

questions.stem: You are evaluating compute and accelerator options on Google Cloud for several machine learning training workloads. Following Google Cloud best practices, which workload is best suited to run on Cloud TPUs?
questions.key: A large-scale recommendation model with fixed tensor shapes and massive embedding tables that trains for several weeks using large batch sizes and standard framework operations.

questions.stem:
You maintain an online prediction service deployed to an endpoint on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You need to roll out a new version of your model to replace the model currently serving production traffic on that endpoint. 

Your solution must satisfy the following requirements:
 Reuse the compute resources backing the current deployment to avoid allocating a separate duplicate pool of resources.
 Gradually transition inference traffic to the new model in proportion to the number of ready-to-serve replicas.
Automatically revert to the previous model version if the new model's container fails its health checks.

Which deployment strategy should you use?
questions.key: Submit a deployModel request to the endpoint that includes rolloutOptions specifying the current deployment's ID as previousDeployedModel along with surge and unavailability thresholds.

questions.stem:
You are deploying a custom-trained machine learning model to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for low-latency online predictions. The model requires custom input preprocessing (feature normalization) and custom postprocessing (converting probabilities into business-specific alert categories). Additionally, clients will submit inference requests formatted as raw CSV instead of standard JSON. Your team wants to test and debug the container locally before deployment, while avoiding the overhead of writing an HTTP model server or creating a Dockerfile from scratch.

How should you package and deploy this solution?
questions.key: Use custom prediction routines by implementing a custom Handler to deserialize the raw CSV requests and a custom Predictor to run inference preprocessing and postprocessing. Build the container using LocalModel.build_cpr_model in the Agent Platform SDK for Python, test it locally with deploy_to_local_endpoint, and upload the model to Model Registry.

questions.stem: You have deployed a custom containerized model to a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform online prediction endpoint using dedicated CPU compute resources (DedicatedResources). During peak traffic hours, incoming request volume surges, leading to queue delays and high latency. However, because the container performs I/O-bound external API lookups during inference, instance CPU utilization remains around 25%, well below the default 60% autoscaling target threshold, so the endpoint does not scale out. You need to reconfigure the serving backend to automatically scale out additional replicas based on incoming request throughput. What should you do?
questions.key: Update the deployment's autoscalingMetricSpecs to use the metric aiplatform.googleapis.com/prediction/online/request_count and set an integer target threshold for requests per minute per replica.

questions.stem:
Your team is building an automated machine learning workflow on Google Cloud that performs data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and deployment. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:
Use a fully managed, serverless orchestration service to run the tasks as a directed acyclic graph (DAG).
Automatically capture and store pipeline artifact lineage and execution metadata in Agent Platform ML Metadata.
Define reusable pipeline components in Python.
Follow the documented lifecycle for defining, compiling, and running pipelines on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

Which architecture and workflow should you implement?
questions.key: Define the workflow and tasks using the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK, compile the pipeline into a YAML intermediate representation file using kfp.compiler.Compiler(), and run the pipeline on Agent Platform Pipelines by creating an aiplatform.PipelineJob that specifies the compiled YAML file and a Cloud Storage pipeline_root.

questions.stem:
You are developing a generative AI prototype in a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench notebook. You need to prototype with an open-source Gemma model available in Model Garden. Your notebook workflow must programmatically list deployable model versions, inspect Model Garden's verified deployment configurations (including recommended machine types and accelerator types), and deploy the model directly to a prediction endpoint using the Vertex AI SDK for Python.

What should you do in your notebook?
questions.key: Import model_garden from vertexai. Call model_garden.list_deployable_models to locate the model ID, instantiate model_garden.OpenModel with the model ID, call list_deploy_options() to inspect verified machine and accelerator configurations, and call deploy() to deploy the model to an endpoint.

questions.stem:
Your team serves a machine learning model for online inference as a Cloud Run service. You have packaged a new model version into a container image and want to perform a canary deployment using Cloud Deploy to compare the performance and reliability of the new model revision against the current production revision with live traffic before fully rolling it out. You want Cloud Deploy to manage progressive traffic shifting automatically.

How should you configure the Cloud Run service manifest and the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline?
questions.key: Provide the Cloud Run service manifest without a traffic stanza. In the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline, configure the stage strategy with runtimeConfig.cloudRun.automaticTrafficControl: true and define the incremental traffic percentages in canaryDeployment.percentages without including 100.

questions.stem: Your company runs a TensorFlow recommendation model for an online store whose catalog and traffic are growing. The training job learns normalization statistics and category mappings from historical purchases. A separate prediction service applies preprocessing through code maintained by another team. Recent releases have produced different transformed values for the same product records in training and serving. You want to keep preprocessing consistent as the catalog grows while minimizing duplicate maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Use TensorFlow Transform to learn preprocessing from training data, train on its transformed outputs, and embed the transformation graph in the exported model for serving.

questions.stem:
Your team is deploying a multi-turn customer support chatbot powered by a Large Language Model (LLM) on Google Cloud. You need to implement Model Armor to protect the system from prompt injection and jailbreak attacks on user inputs, while preventing the model from leaking credentials and returning malicious URLs in its outputs.

Following Google Cloud best practices for Model Armor, how should you configure the templates and prepare the prompt sanitization payloads?
questions.key: Configure separate Model Armor templates for user prompts and model responses. For each interaction, send only the latest user message in the prompt sanitization request, excluding conversation history and system prompts.

questions.stem: You need to monitor a retailer's delivery-time predictor as growing order volume brings new service areas. The model runs on Agent Platform, but its training data reflects an older delivery network. Production trip distances have differed from training for months, and prediction quality has remained stable. You want to detect new changes in incoming delivery features while minimizing alerts caused by those longstanding differences. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure Agent Platform Model Monitoring to compare current input feature distributions with a recent, representative production baseline. Investigate drift alerts for trip distance and other delivery features as order volume grows.

questions.stem:
Your organization has deployed a customer support generative AI agent into production using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. To ensure consistent agent performance, the machine learning engineering team needs to implement continuous monitoring to detect quality drift and safety degradation across live customer interactions. The solution must evaluate live production conversations asynchronously without introducing latency to user-facing requests, and it must allow the team to manage evaluation costs by bounding the volume of evaluated interactions.

Which approach should you take?
questions.key: Configure an Online Monitor in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with Cloud Trace enabled, select the desired evaluation metrics, and set a sampling percentage and maximum samples per run.

questions.stem: You are building an automated quality control solution on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You need to adapt a foundation model using supervised fine-tuning to perform visual inspection and identify subtle manufacturing defects from component photos stored in Cloud Storage. You must configure the dataset and tuning job so that the model captures high visual detail while adhering to supported platform specifications. How should you prepare the training dataset and configure the tuning job?
questions.key: Create a JSONL dataset where each example specifies user contents with fileData referencing the Cloud Storage URIs and model contents with the expected defect descriptions, and set mediaResolution to MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH in the generationConfig.

questions.stem:
You are designing a feature management architecture using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Store. Your machine learning model requires features consolidated from two separate BigQuery tables: customer_demographics and customer_activity. Both BigQuery tables contain historical records for the same entity ID (customer_id) tracked over time using a feature_timestamp column. You need to serve the latest combined feature values from both sources for real-time online inference, while preserving historical values in BigQuery for model training.

How should you configure the Feature Store resources?
questions.key: Create a separate FeatureGroup for each BigQuery table, create the required Feature resources under each group associated with their corresponding columns, and then create a FeatureView within an online store instance that references both FeatureGroups.

questions.stem:
Your team serves a PyTorch recommendation model as an online inference service hosted on Cloud Run. You have packaged an updated model into a new container image and want to perform a canary deployment to compare the new model version against the current production model under live traffic. You need to configure Cloud Deploy to manage the progressive rollout, automatically apportioning traffic across 20% and 50% increments before completing the full rollout to 100%.

How should you configure the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline and Cloud Run service manifest?
questions.key: In the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline stage, configure strategy.canary.runtimeConfig.cloudRun.automaticTrafficControl: true and set canaryDeployment.percentages to [20, 50]. In the Cloud Run service definition manifest, omit the traffic stanza.

questions.stem:
Your team is preparing a supervised fine-tuning dataset to adapt a Gemini 3 model for automated visual quality inspection of printed circuit boards. The training examples include multi-image inputs: zoomed-in detail shots where high visual detail is essential to identify subtle soldering defects, and broad contextual shots where low visual fidelity is sufficient. To keep the training run within your token budget, you need to minimize token consumption without modifying the physical pixel dimensions of the source images stored in Cloud Storage.

How should you configure the dataset?
questions.key: Set the global mediaResolution to MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW in the generationConfig object, and configure mediaResolution with MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH on individual media Part objects for the zoomed-in defect images.

questions.stem: You recently started building a customer support assistant that answers refund questions using retrieved company policies. Your team has several prompt and retrieval configurations to compare, and policy specialists can prepare approved answers for a representative set of customer questions. You want to identify configurations that give accurate answers grounded in those policies while minimizing manual evaluation work. What should you do?
questions.key: Evaluate candidate responses in Agent Platform using representative questions, approved answers, and retrieved policies. Score correctness and grounding with model-based metrics, compare automated scores with specialist ratings on a reviewed subset, and select the configuration with the strongest overall validated results.

questions.stem:
You are designing a feature serving architecture using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Store. Your organization maintains customer features across two separate BigQuery tables:
customer_profiles, containing customer demographic attributes.
customer_behavior_metrics, containing rolling aggregate metrics.

Both BigQuery tables contain historical feature updates over time for each customer ID, tracked using a feature_timestamp column. You need to consolidate specific feature columns from both tables into a single online store endpoint to serve the latest feature values with low latency for online predictions, while preserving historical feature data in BigQuery for model training.

What should you do?
questions.key: Create a separate feature group in the Feature Registry for each BigQuery table, create individual feature resources for the required columns under each feature group, and then create a feature view in the online store instance that associates both feature groups and their respective feature IDs.

questions.stem:
You are prototyping a generative AI application inside a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench notebook. You need to evaluate an open-source Gemma model available in Model Garden. Your workflow must satisfy the following requirements:
Programmatically inspect the verified machine type and accelerator deployment options directly from the notebook.
Deploy the model to a managed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform endpoint from the notebook without manually specifying custom container definitions or downloading and managing checkpoint artifacts.
Submit inference requests directly to the deployed endpoint to validate model responses.

Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Import vertexai.model_garden, instantiate the model with model_garden.OpenModel, view the verified deployment specifications with list_deploy_options(), deploy the model using model.deploy(), and invoke predictions using endpoint.predict().

questions.stem: You are operating an insurance assistant recently deployed to draft claim summaries from adjusters' notes and retrieved records. A production review found instructions embedded in claim notes that redirected the assistant's replies. Reviewers also found sensitive claimant details reaching the model and appearing in summaries intended for broader distribution. You want to protect claimant confidentiality while minimizing ongoing maintenance of application safeguards. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Integrate Model Armor before model calls and summary distribution, combining prompt injection detection with Sensitive Data Protection to block detected malicious content and redact sensitive values.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose recently deployed Gemini assistant summarizes claim notes for adjusters. After optimizing prompts, the service still omits required domain wording, and 5,000 approved prompt-and-summary pairs are already stored in BigQuery. You want to teach Gemini the desired summaries directly from that table by using SQL, evaluate the tuned result for this use case, and minimize data preparation and training-application development. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a supported Gemini model, perform supervised tuning by selecting the prompt and label columns from the BigQuery table, and assess the tuned model with the EVALUATE function.

questions.stem: You work for a publisher that is migrating an existing manual-translation workload to Google Cloud. Every night it translates 60 native PDF product manuals into three languages, but its OCR-and-plain-text workflow discards layout and produces PDFs that editors cannot revise easily. The source files are available only as native PDFs. You want to produce editable DOCX translations while retaining as much formatting as possible, process the nightly set in one managed request, and avoid custom code that reconstructs each document’s layout. What should you do?
questions.key: Store the native PDFs in Cloud Storage and submit one batch Document Translation request for all three target languages. Configure the batch request to convert the native PDF outputs to DOCX.

questions.stem: You work for an electronics manufacturer whose running Gemini 3 inspection system analyzes a close-up and a wider context photo for each circuit board. It still misses small solder defects, and using high resolution for every training image consumes too many tokens. You want to adapt the model to your labeled defect examples while minimizing image tokens without losing detail from the close-ups. What should you do?
questions.key: Fine-tune Gemini with supervised learning. Use high media resolution for each close-up part and low global media resolution for the remaining images.

questions.stem:
You are an ML engineer building a real-time recommendation service. Feature data is maintained in two separate BigQuery tables: user_demographics and user_behavior_metrics, both sharing the same entity ID column user_id. You need to accomplish the following:
Consolidate specific feature columns from both BigQuery tables into a single endpoint for online serving.
Enable feature monitoring to detect feature drift and retrieve feature statistics.
Ensure features can be discovered and reused across multiple modeling projects.

How should you configure Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Store to meet these requirements?
questions.key: Create a separate FeatureGroup resource for each BigQuery table, associating each group with its respective table. Create Feature resources within each feature group mapped to the specific BigQuery columns. Then, create a single FeatureView in an online store instance that references both feature groups and their respective feature IDs from the Feature Registry.

questions.stem:
You are developing a generative AI prototype within a Jupyter notebook on a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench instance. You want to evaluate an open-source model available in Model Garden (such as a Gemma 3 model). You need to programmatically inspect the verified deployment hardware configurations (machine type and accelerator specifications) for the model and deploy it to a dedicated endpoint directly within Python.

Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Import model_garden from vertexai, initialize an instance using model_garden.OpenModel, call list_deploy_options() on the model object to view verified deployment specifications, and call deploy() to create the endpoint.

questions.stem:
You have an online machine learning prediction service deployed as a container on Cloud Run. You have trained a new version of the model and want to implement a canary deployment strategy using Cloud Deploy to compare the performance and reliability of the new model against the existing version on a subset of live production traffic (25% and 50%) before routing 100% of traffic to it. You want Cloud Deploy to automatically manage the traffic shifting between the revisions.

How should you configure the Cloud Run service manifest and the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline?
questions.key: Define the Cloud Run service manifest without a traffic stanza. In the Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline configuration, set runtimeConfig.cloudRun.automaticTrafficControl: true under strategy.canary, and define canaryDeployment.percentages with [25, 50].

questions.stem:
You are designing an ML feature management architecture using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Store. Your team maintains feature data across two separate BigQuery tables: one containing customer demographic attributes and the other containing customer behavioral aggregations. Both tables contain historical records over time with multiple rows per customer entity ID, formatted as a time series using a feature_timestamp column. 

You need to consolidate features from both tables into a single endpoint to serve the latest feature values for low-latency online predictions, while preserving the ability to retrieve point-in-time historical feature values for offline model training. 

What should you do?
questions.key: Create a FeatureGroup resource associated with each BigQuery table, create Feature resources corresponding to the required columns within each FeatureGroup, and then create a FeatureView in an online store instance that references both feature groups.

questions.stem: Your company is migrating a customer-retention classifier from Cloud Run to Agent Platform. Several retention applications call the current service, where Python code encodes account attributes before XGBoost prediction and maps scores to risk labels afterward. The transformations work in production, and your team has representative requests and responses for migration checks. You want to preserve the classifier's request and response behavior while minimizing custom serving-code maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Implement custom prediction routines that reuse the Python preprocessing, XGBoost prediction, and postprocessing in a Predictor. Build the container with Agent Platform SDK for Python, check local inference against representative requests and responses, and deploy to an endpoint.

questions.stem: You work for a bank whose fraud model uses customer and transaction features stored in separate BigQuery tables. After a security incident, you discover that the project’s default service account lets any user who can create a feature group access its BigQuery source. You want teams to discover and reuse selected features through Agent Platform Feature Store, combine features from both tables for online predictions, and restrict access to each source. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a feature group with a dedicated service account for each BigQuery table, register the selected columns as features, and create one feature view from both feature groups using a dedicated service account.

questions.stem: You work for a lender that recently deployed a BigQuery ML boosted-tree classifier to help prioritize loan applications for review. Reviewers now need to understand how each feature affected an individual application’s score, and the risk team needs an overall view of feature influence across the evaluation data. You want to provide both views while retaining the deployed boosted-tree model because it meets your predictive-quality target. What should you do?
questions.key: Run ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT for individual applications and ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN for the evaluation data, using the boosted tree’s Tree SHAP explanations.

questions.stem: You lead machine learning for an online retailer whose nightly transformer training currently runs on CPU VMs and delays pricing updates. The team is migrating to either NVIDIA GPU or Google TPU clusters. Advertised peak specifications point in different directions, and the model might use each platform differently. You want to choose using the current model’s observed distributed-training performance while minimizing accelerator cost, and you want the comparison to expose efficiency losses as the cluster grows. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark the same model on the smallest viable GPU and TPU clusters, compare tokens per second per chip and per dollar, and repeat the benchmark at increasing cluster sizes to measure scaling degradation.

questions.stem: You are managing demand forecasts that a grocery retailer uses to set store replenishment orders. The running model on Agent Platform Inference uses fitted feature transformations before inference and converts predictions into item quantities afterward. As more stores request forecasts, your team has moved these steps into a revised serving container. The model weights are unchanged, and production traffic will switch soon. You want to preserve forecast values while minimizing rollout errors. What should you do?
questions.key: Test the revised container in staging with representative raw requests and expected final item quantities. Compare preprocessing and postprocessing results with the existing pipeline, and approve the change when they match.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose recommendation model already serves production requests through a Cloud Run service. Serving costs have risen, and the team has produced a leaner revision intended to lower prediction latency. Offline results look promising, but product owners want evidence from live traffic before a full release. You want to keep the service on Cloud Run, compare the revisions by first sending 10% of requests to the new revision, and then increase traffic in stages only when performance is acceptable, while minimizing manual traffic changes and user impact. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary for the existing Cloud Run service with a 10% phase followed by larger percentage phases. Use deploy analysis during the canary phases and rollout-advance automation before reaching the stable phase.

questions.stem: You lead ML engineering for a logistics company whose running Agent Platform endpoint prioritizes delayed shipments. After a security incident exposed untraceable requests, company policy requires the serving layer to inspect a request header before scoring. Existing systems send CSV records and cannot be changed. You also want the serving layer to normalize inputs and convert model scores into operational priority labels, while avoiding a hand-built HTTP server or Dockerfile and preserving local testing. What should you do?
questions.key: Build a custom inference routine with a custom Handler and Predictor. Use the Handler for the request header and CSV handling, and the Predictor for normalization, inference, and priority-label postprocessing.

questions.stem: You work for an online retailer building a custom recommendation model that will rank products during checkout. The serving path needs proprietary request preprocessing, and launch traffic is expected to swing from quiet periods to sharp bursts. In prototype tests, the model server returned HTTP success before its weights were fully loaded. You want capacity to add replicas as throughput rises while preventing requests from reaching a new replica until the model is ready, and you don't want to remove the preprocessing. What should you do?
questions.key: Package the preprocessing and model server in an Agent Platform custom container, push the image to Artifact Registry, import the model, and deploy it to an endpoint using non-TPU autoscaling replicas. Configure a custom health probe that succeeds only after the model is fully loaded.

questions.stem: You work for a claims company that runs a customer-service assistant. Production monitoring shows repeated prompts that try to override the assistant’s instructions, and reviewers have found proprietary case identifiers in some model replies. You want to block injection attempts before they reach the model and prevent custom case identifiers from reaching customers, while keeping input and output policies independently tunable. What should you do?
questions.key: Create separate Model Armor templates for inputs and outputs. Use prompt injection and jailbreak detection with Inspect and block for each new user message, and use advanced Sensitive Data Protection with inspection and de-identification for every model response before returning the sanitized text.

questions.stem: You run an online travel company whose production assistant handles multi-turn booking conversations. After migrating the already-running assistant to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, you need to replace manual quality reviews. You want to continuously detect declining response quality and safety as customer behavior changes, evaluate a controlled sample of live conversations to limit evaluation cost, and let engineers inspect the score and rationale for an individual interaction. What should you do?
questions.key: Enable Cloud Trace and export the required agent and inference telemetry. Create an Online Monitor that samples live traces, applies quality and safety metrics, caps samples per run, and reports results to the evaluation dashboard and individual trace views.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose support application already calls Gemini from BigQuery to draft case resolutions. The model repeatedly misses company-specific resolution patterns, while long few-shot prompts increase inference latency and cost. Hundreds of approved prompt-and-answer pairs are stored in BigQuery. Your analysts want to tune Gemini directly from these rows with SQL, without exporting them to files, and evaluate the tuned model before changing production. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a supported Gemini model, use the BigQuery prompt-and-answer columns as supervised tuning data, and evaluate the tuned model before switching production.

questions.stem: You are operating product recommendation models for an online retailer. Several models use the same customer purchase aggregates, but training jobs and prediction services calculate them independently from transaction data in BigQuery. As traffic grows, these repeated calculations increase serving latency and processing costs. Your team already uses Agent Platform Feature Store for other customer features. You want to reuse consistent purchase features across training and serving while minimizing repeated computation. What should you do?
questions.key: Materialize purchase aggregates in one BigQuery feature table and register them in Agent Platform Feature Store. Use the table for training and a synchronized feature view for online serving.

questions.stem: Your company uses an XGBoost model to estimate delivery times at checkout. Monitoring shows that identical shipment details receive different estimates across applications. The model runs in an Agent Platform prebuilt container, while each client separately transforms shipment features and converts predicted log delivery times into hours. These client implementations have diverged. You want consistent input and output processing across clients while minimizing the code your team needs to implement and maintain. What should you do?
questions.key: Package the existing model with shared preprocessing and postprocessing using custom inference routines. Test the container locally against the training pipeline's transformations, then deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint.

questions.stem: You need to improve feature retrieval for a grocery delivery estimator your team recently deployed. Two BigQuery tables contain store preparation and courier availability features, both keyed by delivery zone. Each table is registered as a separate feature group in Agent Platform Feature Store. The application currently fetches separate feature views and joins their results for each estimate. You want to retrieve combined features with low latency while minimizing maintenance of duplicate feature data. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a consolidated feature view in Agent Platform Feature Store using the required features from both existing feature groups. Sync the view, then update the estimator to fetch combined features by delivery zone.

questions.stem: You work for an appliance manufacturer building a localization service for product manuals. Writers place up to 100 DOCX and PPTX files for each release in Cloud Storage, and the release team needs versions in three languages. Approved product names must remain consistent in every translation. You want to translate each release in one request while preserving the documents’ formatting and layout and applying the approved terminology. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Cloud Translation - Advanced batch Document Translation with the Cloud Storage files as inputs. Specify the three target languages and apply a glossary for each language.

questions.stem: Your company trains a TensorFlow demand-forecasting model each night to guide store replenishment. The dense neural network runs on a GPU, and training accounts for most of the forecasting workflow's compute bill. Stores receive forecasts each morning, and the team uses an existing validation target to judge model quality. You want to reduce training cost while minimizing missed morning forecast deadlines. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark representative end-to-end training runs on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs to the existing validation target. Select the lowest-cost configuration that reaches the target before the morning forecast deadline.

questions.stem: You work for an online retailer whose recently deployed Gemini application extracts product attributes from catalog photos. It handles common products, but it often misses the retailer’s specialized categories and terminology. Your team has representative images paired with the correct structured descriptions in Cloud Storage. You want to improve accuracy for this specialized image-understanding task by teaching the model from those examples, while keeping image analysis rather than generating new images. What should you do?
questions.key: Fine-tune a supported Gemini model with supervised learning on the labeled image-and-description examples, and use the tuned model for the catalog extraction workload.

questions.stem: You recently expanded an online retailer's recommendation service to new customer segments, and shopper traffic is growing. The application serves the current model, and your team has deployed a candidate separately after promising offline results. Changes in the shopper mix make historical purchase rates difficult to compare. You want to measure the candidate's effect on purchases while minimizing bias from the changing traffic mix. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Randomly assign shoppers to stable cohorts with App Lifecycle Manager feature flags, route each cohort to one deployment, and record purchases by cohort. Compare concurrent purchase rates before selecting the model version to retain.

questions.stem: You manage a retailer’s running fraud-scoring model, whose offline features remain in two BigQuery tables. After unexpected scoring changes, the risk team wants feature statistics and drift detection, while other ML teams want the same features in a shared registry. You want to expose selected columns from both tables through one online feature view without duplicating the offline data. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a feature group for each BigQuery table, add the selected columns as features in their respective groups, and create one feature view that includes features from both groups.

questions.stem: You are maintaining a recently deployed Gemini assistant that summarizes warranty claims for service agents. Your team fine-tunes candidates using approved claim summaries in BigQuery. The latest candidate has lower training loss, and BigQuery contains another set of representative claims paired with approved summaries that the team set aside for model review. You want to reduce summary corrections while minimizing additional tuning compute. What should you do?
questions.key: Compare the candidate and deployed model on reserved claims for accuracy and completeness, and promote the candidate only if its summaries improve.

questions.stem: You work for an online retailer whose fraud model serves live checkout requests on Cloud Run. After a recent deployment, your team produced another model version that performed better in offline tests. You want to keep the service on Cloud Run, compare the current and candidate revisions under production traffic, and expose only a small share of requests to the candidate at first. If its monitored performance remains acceptable, you want traffic to increase in stages with minimal manual work. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary for the Cloud Run service with several traffic-percentage phases. Use deploy analysis on the canary phases and automate advancement when the monitored performance is acceptable.

questions.stem: You work for a subscription business whose retention team uses an existing BigQuery ML boosted-tree regression model to prioritize customer outreach. Account managers review each customer’s feature contributions, while the risk committee reviews feature influence across the full evaluation dataset. As scoring volume has grown, exact Tree SHAP explanations take too long. You want to keep the boosted-tree model and preserve both individual and overall explanations while reducing explanation time. What should you do?
questions.key: Use approximate feature contribution with ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT for individual predictions and ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN for overall feature influence.

questions.stem: You are running a loan-default classifier on Agent Platform for a lender that uses scores to prioritize application reviews. As traffic grows and serving capacity expands, checks show that replicas produce different model input vectors for identical applications. Training uses fitted numeric normalization and categorical encoding artifacts, but inference preprocessing maintains its transformations separately. You want consistent inference inputs across replicas while minimizing retraining. What should you do?
questions.key: Reuse the training-fitted normalization and encoding artifacts in each replica's inference preprocessing. Validate raw-application transformations against a fixed set of training-reference examples.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose running Gemini assistant classifies incoming claims for routing.
