After a security incident, company policy no longer allows examples from past claims to appear in production prompts. The team already optimized the prompt, but recurrent classification errors remain. You have 600 high-quality labeled examples that match production requests. You want to improve consistency using only this dataset while removing the examples from prompts and minimizing the compute required for training. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Agent Platform supervised fine-tuning with the labeled examples, selecting a supported Gemini model and a parameter-efficient tuning approach.

questions.stem: You need to build a demand forecasting service for a retailer's replenishment application. Warehouse planners will use its forecasts to decide how much stock to order. The custom-trained forecasting model is ready, and the application backend runs in a Google Cloud VPC. Your team already uses Agent Platform for managed model deployment. You want to keep prediction access within the application's private network while minimizing serving infrastructure maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Deploy the forecasting model to an Agent Platform private endpoint using Private Service Connect, and connect the application's VPC to its service attachment through a forwarding rule for prediction requests.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose running demand-forecasting model guides inventory purchases. As the business grows, your team retrains more frequently. The current release is registered in Agent Platform Model Registry, but newer artifacts accumulate in storage directories, and a shared spreadsheet tracks the production release. You want to retain identifiable releases with clear references to production and candidate versions while minimizing manual release bookkeeping. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Register each retrained artifact as a new version of the existing Agent Platform Model Registry model and assign production and candidate aliases.

questions.stem: You are tuning a payment processor's fraud classifier as transaction volume grows. The running model is approaching its serving capacity, and your team has produced several candidates through retraining and model compression. Fraudulent transactions make up a small fraction of traffic. You have labeled transactions held out from training and recorded production traffic available for testing. You want to increase serving throughput while minimizing missed fraud. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark each candidate on the serving hardware using representative production traffic, and measure fraud recall on held-out transactions. Select a candidate that increases throughput while matching or exceeding the current production model's recall.

questions.stem: You are reducing inspection delays for a manufacturer whose image-based defect detection service runs on Agent Platform. Preprocessing resizes and normalizes images, and postprocessing converts model scores into pass-or-fail decisions. The existing model performs well. Your team has proposed faster implementations of both transformations, with promising results from isolated timing tests. You want to preserve defect-detection quality while minimizing prediction latency. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark the current and proposed inference pipelines in staging on representative labeled raw images. Compare final pass-or-fail decisions, detection quality, and end-to-end latency before adopting the faster transformations.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose fraud model is already serving online predictions on Agent Platform. Monitoring after a claims-system update shows failed requests because the system now sends CSV rows, and that system cannot be changed. Each request also needs a current customer-status lookup from an external service and the model’s input normalization; adjusters need a low, medium, or high risk result instead of a probability. You want to test this request-time logic locally while minimizing web-serving and container-build work. What should you do?
questions.key: Build a custom inference routine. Use a custom Handler to deserialize the CSV request, and implement preprocessing and postprocessing in the Predictor. Test it with a local endpoint, then upload the model to Model Registry and deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint.

questions.stem: Your company runs a delivery-time prediction service that retrieves current driver workload features from Agent Platform Feature Store. Feature jobs update workload throughout the day and retain timestamped history in BigQuery. As delivery volume grows, your team expands training to several months of orders, but the pipeline attaches each driver's most recent workload values to every historical order. You want training features to reflect what was available at each prediction time while minimizing changes to the running feature-serving system. What should you do?
questions.key: Join historical orders to BigQuery feature history using point-in-time lookups, selecting each driver's latest workload values available at the prediction time. Keep Agent Platform Feature Store serving current values for live predictions.

questions.stem: You operate a customer-support assistant that is already serving users. During a security incident, an attacker used a prompt-injection message, and the assistant returned a proprietary customer identifier. Your security team already maintains Sensitive Data Protection inspect and de-identify templates for that identifier. You want to block malicious prompts before they reach the model and redact the identifier from responses while preserving safe text. You also want to avoid maintaining a second copy of the detection policy. What should you do?
questions.key: Place Model Armor before and after the model. Use an input template with prompt injection and jailbreak detection in inspect-and-block mode, and use an output template with advanced Sensitive Data Protection linked to the existing inspect and de-identify templates; enforce the input verdict and return the de-identified response.

questions.stem: You work for an online travel marketplace building a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform assistant that helps customers change complex itineraries across several conversational turns. You want to verify context retention and conversational flow before launch. After launch, you also want to detect quality drift continuously from live conversations while limiting evaluation spend. The team will deploy the agent on Agent Runtime and export the required agent traces. What should you do?
questions.key: Run an offline Session evaluation on staged conversations with relevant predefined or custom metrics. After launch, create an Online Monitor for the live traces, configure quality metrics, and set a sampling percentage and maximum samples per run.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose recently deployed Gemini model summarizes claim notes for adjusters. The notes remain in BigQuery, where hundreds of rows pair production prompts with approved summaries; each row is already marked for training or evaluation. Despite prompt refinement, the model repeatedly misses the company’s summary style. You want to fine-tune Gemini directly from these tables with SQL, preserve the existing evaluation group, and evaluate the resulting model while avoiding data exports and a custom training application. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a supported Gemini model, use the labeled table as the supervised-tuning input, configure the existing marker as a custom data split, and evaluate the tuned model with the EVALUATE function.

questions.stem: You work for an online retailer whose customer-service assistant runs on a self-deployed open model from Model Garden. Monitoring shows that traffic is unpredictable and bursty, and the team has not customized the model. The current model’s answers no longer meet the support team’s needs. You want to evaluate a standard replacement against the assistant’s task and required features, test its text responses before deployment, and minimize both infrastructure work and evaluation cost. What should you do?
questions.key: In Model Garden, filter candidates by task and required features, review their model cards, test supported candidates with representative prompts in the free demo playground, and select a suitable MaaS model.

questions.stem: You work for a global publisher whose running localization pipeline extracts text from formatted word-processing and presentation documents, translates it, and has staff restore the original design. During migration to Google Cloud, nightly jobs will translate thousands of files from Cloud Storage into several languages. Approved product terms must remain consistent. You want each translation job to accept multiple documents and target languages while preserving layout and minimizing custom reconstruction and manual work. What should you do?
questions.key: Partition the files into supported batch sizes and use Cloud Translation - Advanced batch Document Translation, applying the approved glossary and writing translated documents to Cloud Storage.

questions.stem: You work for a subscription company whose recently deployed BigQuery ML boosted-tree model identifies customers likely to cancel, helping retention agents prioritize outreach. Agents now need to understand which features drove each customer’s prediction, while the compliance team needs an overall view of which features influence predictions across the evaluation data. You want to provide both views while keeping the deployed boosted-tree model in place. What should you do?
questions.key: Keep the boosted-tree model and use BigQuery ML Tree SHAP explanations: run ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT for per-customer feature attributions and ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN for overall feature influence.

questions.stem: Your company is migrating its running support-ticket classifier to a supported Qwen model in Model Garden. Extensive prompt experiments have reached an accuracy plateau on several company-specific categories. You have 600 high-quality tickets paired with correct categories, matching production inputs. The selected model offers both adapter tuning and full fine-tuning. A supported larger teacher model achieves nearly the same classification accuracy as the migration candidate. You want to improve classification accuracy while minimizing tuning costs. What should you do?
questions.key: Run supervised fine-tuning on the selected Qwen model using LoRA and the labeled tickets. Supply a separate validation dataset to evaluate the tuned model.

questions.stem: You recently reviewed the cost of training the language model that generates product descriptions for your online store. The workload currently runs on GPUs. A TPU pilot processed fewer training tokens per second despite advertising higher peak compute performance, and the candidate systems have different prices. You want to identify which hardware provides the most useful training progress per dollar for your workload. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Benchmark the same representative model on GPU and TPU systems using platform-appropriate training software. Compare cost-normalized training throughput, accounting for time lost to hardware faults, network stalls, and checkpoint recovery.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose deployed claims assistant uses Gemini 2.5 Flash to classify adjuster notes. Monitoring shows recurring classification errors despite an optimized prompt, and the long instructions and few-shot examples increase inference latency and cost. You have 800 high-quality labeled examples that match production inputs and expected outputs. You want to reduce the errors and shorten prompts while minimizing tuning and serving costs, without collecting subjective preference data. What should you do?
questions.key: Supervised fine-tune Gemini 2.5 Flash on the labeled examples in Agent Platform, validate the tuned model on held-out examples, and replace the long prompt with shorter task instructions.

questions.stem: You lead ML at an online marketplace. The recommendation model drives product ranking and currently trains on NVIDIA GPU instances, but rising training spend has prompted a possible migration to TPUs. Peak accelerator specifications suggest a clear winner, yet the model and software were optimized for the current platform, and production retraining uses a large distributed cluster. You want to choose the platform with the best real training performance per dollar at production scale while distinguishing hardware limits from model or software mismatch. What should you do?
questions.key: Run compute, memory, and interconnect microbenchmarks and roofline analysis on both platforms. Then hold the model constant, use platform-appropriate training frameworks, and compare TPS per chip per dollar and goodput as each cluster scales to the production size.

questions.stem: You are managing a retailer's recommendation model, recently deployed on a GPU-backed Agent Platform Inference endpoint with a fixed replica count. During promotions, queued requests delay shoppers while GPU utilization stays high and CPU utilization remains low. Between promotions, traffic drops and serving capacity sits idle. You want serving capacity to follow changing request throughput while minimizing the operational work needed to scale the service. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Configure GPU-based autoscaling on the existing endpoint, and validate minimum and maximum replica counts with representative traffic load tests.

questions.stem: You run an online fraud-scoring model for a payments company in a Cloud Run service. A new container version is intended to reduce inference cost and latency, but offline tests do not show how it behaves under production traffic. You want to compare the current and new versions with live requests, begin with a small traffic share, and increase that share in several stages only when observed performance is acceptable, while minimizing manual traffic management. Company policy requires the service to remain on Cloud Run. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure a Cloud Deploy automated canary for the Cloud Run service with several progressively larger traffic percentages. Add deploy analysis to each canary phase and an advance rollout rule so acceptable results automatically move the rollout to the next phase.

questions.stem: You work for an insurer whose running fraud model serves several claims applications. After a security incident exposed raw probability scores, a review found that each client separately converts CSV claims, normalizes features, and maps predictions to risk bands. You want to move those steps into the serving implementation, continue accepting CSV, and test the complete request-to-response flow locally while minimizing custom web-server and container work. What should you do?
questions.key: Build a custom inference routine with a custom Handler that deserializes CSV requests and a Predictor that normalizes features and converts predictions to risk bands. Test it with a local endpoint, then upload it to Model Registry and deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint.

questions.stem: Your company uses a model to estimate delivery arrival times in its customer app. The latest retraining reduced validation error, but production monitoring shows slower prediction responses. Your team has an existing Agent Platform Pipelines workflow, held-out delivery records, and recorded app traffic it can replay. You want to meet the app's prediction response-time target while minimizing delivery-estimation error. What should you do?
questions.key: Tune model complexity across training trials. Measure validation error and tail prediction latency by replaying representative app traffic in staging, then deploy the candidate with the lowest error that meets the response-time target.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose demand-forecasting model drives daily replenishment. A recently deployed workflow still relies on engineers to start data preparation, training, evaluation, and deployment in order, and its artifacts are difficult to trace across runs. You want to run the same workflow every night on a managed, serverless service, enforce dependencies between stages, and retain artifact lineage while avoiding compute that remains allocated between runs. What should you do?
questions.key: Define the stages as dependent Kubeflow Pipelines components, compile the workflow, and create a recurring run with Agent Platform Pipelines. Use Agent Platform ML Metadata for artifact lineage.

questions.stem: You are managing product recommendations for an online retailer. The model runs in an existing Cloud Run service, and request volume has grown as the retailer expands. Your team has prepared a new model version and already collects serving performance metrics in Google Cloud Observability. You want to compare the versions on live traffic at progressively larger shares for the new version while minimizing rollout maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary for the existing Cloud Run service. Use progressively increasing traffic percentages and deploy analysis of performance metrics, combined with rollout advancement automation, to evaluate the model versions before progressing.

questions.stem: You operate an online banking assistant that helps customers understand transactions. It is already in production, and monitoring shows users attempting to override its instructions and pasting account numbers, while some replies contain account identifiers. Company policy does not allow malicious or sensitive inputs to reach the model or sensitive values to reach customers. You want to actively stop all three paths while keeping input and output policies independently tunable. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure separate Model Armor templates for inputs and outputs. Enable prompt injection and jailbreak detection and Sensitive Data Protection on the input template, enable Sensitive Data Protection on the output template, use Inspect and block, and enforce each verdict around the model call.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose production demand forecasts guide inventory replenishment. During a monitoring review, your team struggled to connect a drop in forecast quality to the correct model release. Retraining runs produce new artifacts, but each release has a separate registry entry and approval status lives in a spreadsheet. You want to keep retrained releases together in a traceable model history while minimizing manual bookkeeping. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Register each retrained demand model as a version under one Agent Platform Model Registry entry, and assign movable aliases to identify the approved and previous releases.

questions.stem: You work for a travel company whose customer-support agent is already serving users. Your team has migrated the workload to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and leadership wants to catch declines in response quality, safety, or hallucination rates after the cutover. You want to continuously score a controlled share of live conversations while limiting evaluation cost, and let support engineers inspect the score and rationale for a specific conversation. What should you do?
questions.key: Enable Cloud Trace and the required OpenTelemetry signals for the agent. Create an Online Monitor with the quality and safety metrics, set a sampling percentage and maximum samples per run, and inspect aggregate results in the observability dashboard or individual results in the Traces view.

questions.stem: A travel company recently deployed a Gemini assistant that writes tour descriptions. Reviewers still correct recurring wording errors after several prompt revisions. A BigQuery table contains 400 package prompts paired with approved descriptions, and a Boolean column marks 80 rows reserved for evaluation. You want Gemini to learn from these corrections while minimizing changes to the team's existing SQL workflow. You also want the reserved rows used for evaluation during tuning. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model for supervised tuning of a supported Gemini model. Select the prompt–description pairs as training input and use the reviewers' marker for a custom evaluation split.

questions.stem: You recently started building an image-search service for an online retailer. Your team has trained a prototype neural network that converts uploaded product photos into embeddings and is choosing hardware for the new serving backend. Requests will arrive individually, with short bursts during promotions. You want to keep the 95th-percentile inference latency below 200 milliseconds while minimizing serving compute cost. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark compatible CPU, GPU, and TPU serving configurations using individual requests and representative promotional bursts. Choose the configuration with the lowest total serving compute cost that meets the 95th-percentile latency target.

questions.stem: Extracting text and paragraph boundaries from scanned warranty forms supports a retailer's claims application. The team is migrating its running OCR workload from Vision API to Document AI. Batch jobs read scans from a Cloud Storage bucket in another project within the same organization, and the downstream parser expects Vision API responses. You want to keep that parser working while minimizing migration changes. Company policy does not allow document storage or processing outside the European Union. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Create an EU Document AI Document OCR processor and use its EU endpoint for batch processing. Grant its service agent Storage Object Viewer on the source bucket, and convert results with Document AI Toolbox before passing them to the existing parser.

questions.stem: Your retailer's recommendation service retrieves online scoring features and historical training features through Agent Platform Feature Store. After a security incident exposed broad access to feature sources, you're rebuilding its feature setup. Two teams maintain timestamped histories in separate BigQuery tables in the United States, and scoring depends on their corrections to existing records. You want to consolidate the teams' training and serving features while minimizing upkeep. Company policy allows only approved feature-processing identities to access the source tables. What should you do?
questions.key: Register each table in a feature group with a dedicated service account and add its feature columns. Combine both groups in a feature view with a dedicated service account, restrict source permissions to approved identities, and use scheduled sync.

questions.stem: Prototype a reply-writing assistant for a travel company's support team using open foundation models. The company has a Google Cloud project under its organization and a new Agent Platform Workbench instance. You have sample conversations for adapting the models, and you expect to revise the training code as you explore several candidates in Model Garden. You want to fine-tune the candidates interactively in notebooks while minimizing setup work. What should you do first?
questions.key: Open each supported candidate's model card in Model Garden, choose Open notebook, and adapt the provided tuning notebook in Agent Platform Workbench.

questions.stem: An online retailer uses a recommendation model served by an existing Cloud Run service. A candidate model is intended to reduce response latency, and the team already collects latency metrics in Google Cloud Observability. You want to compare the versions on a small share of live requests before gradually expanding the candidate's traffic. You also want latency results to govern rollout advancement while minimizing traffic-management work. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary for the existing Cloud Run service. Use progressive traffic percentages, deploy analysis of latency during canary phases, and rollout-advance automation.

questions.stem: Your insurer's claims application uses a scikit-learn model on an Agent Platform online endpoint. The claims system submits comma-separated records, and the model expects normalized features. After a security incident exposed internal prediction details, client responses are now restricted to an approved risk category. You want to apply input transformations and response filtering to each request while minimizing model-server maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Build custom inference routines with a Handler for record deserialization and a Predictor for normalization and risk-category postprocessing. Use Agent Platform SDK for Python to build and test the container locally.

questions.stem: You are assessing answer quality for a retailer's customer-support agent as its running deployment migrates to Agent Platform. The agent uses a fully managed Gemini model, Cloud Trace is enabled, and the telemetry needed for evaluation is already being exported. Customer traffic varies sharply during promotions. You want ongoing quality scores from live conversations while keeping evaluation workload bounded as traffic grows. What should you do?
questions.key: Create an Online Monitor with response-quality metrics. Sample live traces and set a maximum number of samples per run to bound the evaluation workload.

questions.stem: Your company's security operations assistant uses a Llama model from Model Garden to classify incident reports. A recent security incident exposed recurring errors in company-specific categories despite extensive prompt refinement. The model supports both full and parameter-efficient tuning, and analysts have prepared 600 carefully labeled complete reports representative of production traffic. You want more reliable classification while minimizing tuning compute. Company policy requires all tuning resources to stay in the Netherlands. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Run region-specific managed supervised fine-tuning of the Llama model in the Netherlands using LoRA and the analyst-labeled reports, then evaluate it on complete incident reports.

questions.stem: An online retailer serves product recommendations from a model running on Cloud Run. Your team recently prepared a release containing a new model version, and the current version still handles customer requests. You want to compare the versions on live traffic through progressively larger canary shares, with advancement based on latency and error-rate checks. You also want Cloud Deploy to manage traffic balancing and phase advancement for you. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary for the existing service with progressive traffic percentages, deploy analysis for the metric checks, and an automatic phase-advancement rule.

questions.stem: You score loan applications with a running custom model and are migrating its serving backend to Agent Platform on Cloud TPU. The existing TPU-ready container has separate scoring and explanation routes that clients will continue using. Load tests show that four replicas handle peak throughput. During startup, the server reports healthy before loading the model. You want enough serving capacity for peak traffic while minimizing failed requests during startup. What should you do?
questions.key: Deploy the TPU-ready container with four minimum replicas. Enable arbitrary custom-route forwarding and configure a health probe that succeeds only after the model is loaded.

questions.stem: An online retailer serves product recommendations through an existing Cloud Run service. A candidate model responds faster in internal tests, and the team already collects latency and error-rate metrics in Google Cloud Observability. You want to compare the two model versions on live traffic, starting with a small share for the candidate. You want traffic increases to depend on latency and error-rate results while minimizing custom rollout code. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure a Cloud Deploy automated canary for the existing Cloud Run service. Use small initial traffic percentages, latency and error-rate deploy analysis in canary phases, and rollout advancement automation driven by that analysis.

questions.stem: Your company's employee IT support assistant helps troubleshoot network problems through text conversations. Monitoring has uncovered messages containing internal IP addresses and attempts to make the assistant override its safeguards. You want to block detected prompt injection attempts while minimizing rejection of legitimate troubleshooting requests. Company policy allows messages containing internal IP addresses to reach the model only after those addresses are redacted. What should you do?
questions.key: Screen each new message with Model Armor prompt injection and jailbreak detection at high confidence, enforcing block verdicts before model invocation. Use a separate Model Armor template with advanced Sensitive Data Protection inspection and de-identification to redact IP addresses, then forward the sanitized text.

questions.stem: You are maintaining a news publisher's article summarization workflow, which recently began using a Gemini model through BigQuery ML. Editors still correct recurring departures from the publisher's summary style after several rounds of prompt refinement. Your BigQuery table contains 2,000 article prompts paired with editor-approved summaries. You want summaries that better match the editors' examples while minimizing development effort for the training workflow. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a tuning-capable Gemini model, supplying article prompts and approved summaries through AS SELECT for supervised tuning. Evaluate the tuned model before adopting it.

questions.stem: Your team runs a customer-support application that summarizes text conversations for agents. Monitoring shows that its current model often omits the customer's main concern. The shortlisted replacement models in Model Garden offer demo playgrounds and notebook tuning. You want to select a replacement by comparing summaries of representative conversations while minimizing Google Cloud charges for this evaluation. What should you do?
questions.key: Review the candidates' model cards, submit representative conversation prompts through their demo playgrounds, and select the model whose summaries best capture the customer's concern.

questions.stem: You work for a logistics company whose publishing service translates shipping manuals for overseas partners. You are migrating the service to Google Cloud. Authors maintain word-processing and slide originals, which the service converts into publications for distribution. Your team also maintains approved translations for shipping terminology. You want to minimize formatting loss in the translated publications while applying those approved translations. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Translate the word-processing and slide originals with Cloud Translation Advanced Document Translation and a shipping glossary, specifying the source language. Convert the translated documents to PDFs afterward.

questions.stem: You are maintaining a retail recommendation service that uses customer purchase and browsing features. As traffic and the number of model teams grow, the teams maintain features in two BigQuery tables with common customer identifiers and timestamped histories. An Agent Platform Feature Store online store already serves the application. You want teams to discover reusable features in a shared registry while minimizing ongoing work to consolidate their values for predictions. What should you do?
questions.key: Create a feature group for each BigQuery table and register the required columns as features. Create one feature view that selects features from both groups and uses scheduled synchronization in the existing online store.

questions.stem: Your company runs a support-reply assistant, and its growing product catalog has expanded the terminology the assistant encounters. Your team already experiments in Agent Platform Workbench and is considering several open foundation models from Model Garden. You want to explore model-specific tuning code for prototypes using your support examples while minimizing the work to set up those experiments. What should you do first?
questions.key: Open the candidate models' cards in Model Garden and start from their provided tuning notebooks, adapting the examples for the team's Workbench experiments.

questions.stem: You need to build a transaction fraud classifier for a payment processor using historical transactions in BigQuery. Reviewers will use its scores to investigate flagged payments, and model owners will review its behavior across an evaluation dataset. You want to show how each transaction's features contributed to its score relative to a baseline and summarize feature influence across the evaluation dataset. What should you do?
questions.key: Train a boosted tree classifier in BigQuery ML. Use Tree SHAP with ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT for transaction explanations and ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN for the evaluation-dataset summary.

questions.stem: You are training a language model for a customer-support assistant on Compute Engine GPUs. Monitoring shows low accelerator utilization and substantial time spent recovering checkpoints after interrupted runs. Your team is evaluating GPU and TPU hardware for the next training run, but advertised performance figures and initial model benchmarks give different rankings. You want to select the platform that delivers the most useful training progress per dollar. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Benchmark the same representative model on GPUs and TPUs with platform-appropriate optimizations. Compare cost-normalized tokens per second per chip and account for stalls and checkpoint recovery when measuring useful training progress.

questions.stem: Your company uses a recommendation model on Cloud Run to rank products for shoppers. Your team is migrating release management from a manually operated process, and a new model version is ready. You want to compare the current and new versions on live requests at controlled, increasing traffic shares before committing to the replacement, while minimizing manual rollout work. What should you do?
questions.key: Configure an automated Cloud Deploy canary on the existing Cloud Run service. Split traffic progressively, compare version performance using deploy analysis, and automate phase advancement based on that analysis.

questions.stem: You manage a retail replenishment service that uses a scikit-learn model to score inventory shortages. A separate serving application normalizes each request, calls the model, and converts its scores into replenishment priority labels. Maintaining that application's HTTP server and container build has become a growing engineering cost. You want to preserve the service's request and response behavior while minimizing serving infrastructure code maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Agent Platform custom inference routines with a custom Predictor that loads the preprocessor, normalizes inputs, and converts predictions into priority labels. Build the container with the SDK and deploy it to an endpoint.

questions.stem: You are operating a product-image classification service on Agent Platform using Cloud TPU inference nodes. As more stores adopt the service, request volume has grown beyond the capacity of its current replicas. Load tests show that each replica can handle a predictable number of requests per second. You want to increase serving capacity to accommodate the higher throughput. What should you do?
questions.key: Increase the deployed model's minimum replica count, sizing the number of inference nodes from the measured capacity per replica and the service's higher request volume.

questions.stem: You need to track the quality of a customer-support agent that your team recently deployed on Agent Platform. The agent uses a fully managed Gemini model, and Cloud Trace captures the prompts, responses, and other telemetry needed for evaluation. Customers are starting to ask questions that differ from the team's original test cases. You want to continuously detect declining response quality in live conversations while limiting evaluation costs. What should you do?
questions.key: Create an online monitor for the deployed agent using response-quality metrics. Set a sampling percentage and a maximum sample count per run, and review evaluation trends in the agent dashboard.

questions.stem: You manage a news service that uses a foundation model to summarize articles for readers. The service is running, and your team is migrating to a model available in Model Garden. Several candidate text models offer demo playgrounds. You want to select a replacement based on summary quality on representative articles while minimizing charges for the initial comparison. What should you do?
questions.key: Filter Model Garden by task and review candidate model cards. Submit the same representative article prompts to each candidate's demo playground, compare the summaries, and select the model that best fits the task.

questions.stem: Your company translates equipment manuals for overseas customers. Its running workflow converts editable word-processing originals into fixed-layout documents and applies shadow-text removal during every online translation. Customers have reported changes to the manuals' layout, and translation response times have become a concern. The editable originals are still available. You want to preserve the manuals' layout and style more faithfully while reducing translation response latency. What should you do?
questions.key: Translate the editable originals as DOCX files with online Cloud Translation - Advanced Document Translation, then convert the translated results to PDFs.

questions.stem: You are operating a retail recommendation service whose customer features are stored in two BigQuery tables. As more teams adopt the service, they are starting to reuse purchase and browsing features from these tables. Both tables contain timestamped feature histories for the same customer IDs, and data producers sometimes correct existing records in place. An Agent Platform Feature Store online store already uses Bigtable online serving. You want teams to reuse a shared registry of selected features while propagating corrections to online feature values. What should you do?
questions.key: Register each table as a feature group and create features mapped to the selected columns. Combine those features in one feature view in the existing online store, using scheduled sync.

questions.stem: Your company recently deployed a BigQuery ML boosted-tree model that predicts whether players will return to its mobile game. The marketing team uses these predictions to choose players for reengagement campaigns, but its dashboard currently shows only predicted probabilities. You want to explain how each player's features contributed to their prediction relative to a baseline and give campaign managers an overall view of feature influence across the evaluation dataset. What should you do?
questions.key: Use Tree SHAP with ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT on the boosted-tree model for individual players. Use ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN to summarize mean absolute feature attributions across the evaluation dataset.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer that uses an open model from Model Garden to classify customer return requests. Monitoring shows recurring errors on company-specific return categories despite several rounds of prompt improvement. You have 600 carefully labeled examples that reflect production requests. The model supports full and parameter-efficient supervised tuning, as well as distillation. Evaluation shows that a larger teacher model performs about as well as the running model on this task. You want to reduce the recurring classification errors while minimizing tuning cost. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Run parameter-efficient supervised fine-tuning on the existing open model using the carefully labeled return examples. Use LoRA to adapt a subset of its parameters.

questions.stem: You manage training for a language model that summarizes customer support conversations. The job currently runs on GPUs with software tuned for that platform, and your team is evaluating a migration to TPUs. An initial TPU trial processes fewer training tokens per second, even though its advertised compute capacity is higher. You want to identify which accelerator platform will deliver the best training performance per dollar for this workload at the planned production scale. What should you do?
questions.key: Benchmark the same model at the planned scale using platform-optimized GPU and TPU training software. Interpret results with microbenchmarks and roofline analysis, then compare training tokens per second per chip per dollar.

questions.stem: Your company uses a scikit-learn model to forecast product demand for its replenishment application. As more warehouses adopt the service, several applications now repeat the same feature normalization and forecast-to-order conversion around calls to an Agent Platform endpoint. The normalization parameters are saved with the model artifacts. You want to minimize the amount of serving code your team maintains as this logic changes. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Use Agent Platform custom inference routines with a Predictor that inherits from SklearnPredictor. Load the saved normalizer and implement preprocessing and postprocessing, then build and deploy the container using the SDK.

questions.stem: You need to keep your company's online fraud scoring service running as transaction volume grows. The TPU-optimized model currently runs on one Cloud TPU inference replica in Agent Platform. Load tests with the current serving container show that each replica can handle up to 100 requests per second at an acceptable response time. Traffic has grown to a steady 350 requests per second. You want enough serving capacity for this traffic while minimizing idle replicas. What should you do?
questions.key: Increase the deployment's minimum replica count to four, retaining the current TPU machine type and serving container to provide capacity for the measured traffic.

questions.stem: You recently began building a demand-forecasting workflow to help a retailer plan inventory. Each daily run will prepare sales data, train a forecasting model, and evaluate the trained model. Your team has written a Python function for each stage. You want the stages to execute in dependency order while minimizing infrastructure and orchestration maintenance. What should you do?
questions.key: Build Kubeflow Pipelines components from the Python functions, connect task outputs to downstream inputs, and compile the workflow. Use Agent Platform Pipelines to schedule recurring runs of the compiled definition.

questions.stem: You are supporting an IT help-desk assistant that summarizes troubleshooting messages for engineers. Since its recent deployment, users have pasted internal IP addresses into otherwise useful descriptions, and the assistant sends those messages to a language model. You want to replace IP addresses with placeholders before messages reach the model while preserving the remaining troubleshooting text. How should you address this issue?
questions.key: Use a regional Model Armor endpoint to sanitize each text message with advanced Sensitive Data Protection inspection and de-identification templates targeting IP addresses in the same location. Forward the returned de-identified text to the language model.

questions.stem: Your company runs a customer-support agent on Agent Platform. Users have started asking different kinds of questions, and support staff suspect its answers are becoming less useful even though API error rates remain steady. Cloud Trace is enabled, and the agent exports the telemetry needed for evaluation. You want to continuously detect response-quality drift in live conversations while keeping evaluation costs bounded as traffic grows. What should you do?
questions.key: Create an Online Monitor with response-quality metrics, sample a percentage of live traces, and cap samples per run. Review evaluation score trends in the agent dashboard.

questions.stem: You are maintaining a retailer's application that summarizes customer reviews using an open foundation model from Model Garden. Its inference bill has grown, and your team is considering replacement open models. The candidates support demo playgrounds, and you have representative review prompts for comparing their summaries. You want to select a model that handles this task well while minimizing the cost of evaluating candidates. What should you do?
questions.key: Review the candidate model cards in Model Garden. Compare the representative prompts in each model's demo playground, assess how well the summaries fit the application's task, and select the best-performing candidate.

questions.stem: You work for a manufacturer whose translation service produces product manuals for overseas distributors. As more distributors join, the team spends increasing time rebuilding document layouts after translating extracted text. Authors still keep the original editable word-processing documents. You want to preserve the manuals' layout as closely as possible while minimizing custom formatting code. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Translate the original word-processing documents with Cloud Translation Advanced Document Translation, then generate the distribution copies from the translated documents.

questions.stem: Your company runs a Gemma-based assistant that drafts customer support replies using a model from Model Garden. As usage grows across product lines, reviewers collect more examples of replies corrected to match company terminology and support practices. You want the model to learn these task-specific responses from the collected examples while minimizing custom tuning code. What should you do?
questions.key: Open the Gemma model card in Model Garden, launch its fine-tuning pipeline, and create a tuning run in Agent Platform Pipelines using the support examples.

questions.stem: You need to build a customer churn predictor using purchase and support features stored in separate BigQuery tables. Both tables contain timestamped histories for each customer, and the data teams occasionally correct existing records. Your project already has a Bigtable online store in Agent Platform Feature Store. You want to make historical features reusable for training and consolidate the latest source values for online predictions. What should you do?
questions.key: Keep historical training data in BigQuery. Register each table as a feature group, map selected columns to features, and include feature timestamps. Create one feature view from both groups using scheduled synchronization.

questions.stem: You manage a gaming app's player-return prediction model in BigQuery ML. During routine monitoring of the running boosted-tree classifier, your team notices unexpected predictions for several players and begins reviewing those cases. You want to see how each feature changed each player's prediction relative to a baseline, and you want the attribution calculation to be exact. What should you do?
questions.key: Apply ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT with Tree SHAP to the reviewed player records, and inspect each feature's attribution relative to the baseline prediction.

questions.stem: You are maintaining a retailer's replenishment service, which uses a scikit-learn model on an Agent Platform endpoint to predict product demand. As more stores join, client applications are duplicating input normalization and rules that convert forecasts into reorder quantities. You want to centralize these transformations in the model's serving path while minimizing custom serving code. What should you do?
questions.key: Use custom inference routines with a Predictor that inherits model loading and prediction from SklearnPredictor. Implement normalization and reorder calculations in preprocessing and postprocessing, and build the serving container with Agent Platform SDK for Python.

questions.stem: Your company is building a product-image classification service using a custom container on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Load tests of compatible CPU and TPU deployments show that each fully initialized inference node sustains 100 predictions per second. Expected peak demand is 400 predictions per second. You want to provision enough serving capacity for that peak. What should you do?
questions.key: Provision four TPU inference replicas by setting the minimum replica count to four, giving the endpoint sufficient measured capacity for peak traffic.

questions.stem: You are migrating quality monitoring for a customer-support agent that already runs on Agent Platform and answers questions about returns. Your team currently reviews a saved set of conversations after each release. Cloud Trace is enabled, and the deployed agent exports the telemetry needed for evaluation. You want to continuously detect declining response quality as live customer requests change while keeping evaluation costs bounded. What should you do?
questions.key: Create an Online Monitor for the deployed agent with response-quality metrics. Sample live traces, cap samples per run, and review evaluation scores over time in the agent's dashboard.

questions.stem: You recently deployed a support-ticket classifier using an open model from Model Garden. The model supports both adapter tuning and full fine-tuning. In production, the classifier repeatedly confuses company-specific ticket categories. You have 600 expert-labeled tickets that reflect production requests and clearly define the correct categories. You want to improve classification accuracy while minimizing the computational resources needed for tuning. What should you do?
questions.key: Run managed supervised fine-tuning with LoRA on the labeled tickets, adapting a subset of the model's parameters to the company's classification task.

questions.stem: You are maintaining an application that summarizes service reports for field technicians. Routine quality reviews show recurring departures from your company's summary style. BigQuery holds 1,200 report prompts paired with reviewer-approved summaries that reflect production inputs, and your team already uses SQL for its reporting workflow. You want summaries to follow the approved style more consistently while minimizing implementation effort. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a supported Gemini model, selecting stored prompts and approved summaries for supervised tuning. Evaluate the tuned model before using it.

questions.stem: You work for a retailer whose demand-forecasting workflow uses Ray for data preparation and model training. Following a recent deployment on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the workflow repeatedly submits the same short Ray jobs. Measurements show that job startup takes longer than the actual processing. You want to reduce startup overhead while minimizing changes to the existing Ray application. Which approach should you use?
questions.key: Keep a long-running Ray cluster on Agent Platform and submit the existing application repeatedly to reuse available compute and cached data and images.

plan.engineering_decision: Choose how to package an existing PyTorch model’s native dependencies for serving on Agent Platform.
plan.business_consequence: Failed predictions delay insurance claim assessments; restoring the serving runtime lets automated damage scoring resume.
plan.existing_system: Your company uses a PyTorch model to score vehicle damage for insurance claims through an Agent Platform endpoint. Monitoring shows prediction failures after a model update introduced a compiled operator that depends on a native library. The updated model works in the team's custom training image, which starts a training process, but the serving image lacks the required library. You want to restore reliable damage scoring while minimizing changes to the serving infrastructure. What should you do?
decisive_constraints: You want to restore reliable damage scoring while minimizing changes to the serving infrastructure.
plan.best_action: Build a custom prediction container with the model’s native libraries and an inference server, then deploy it to the existing Agent Platform endpoint.

mistakes.action: Deploy a prebuilt PyTorch prediction container to the existing Agent Platform endpoint, and include the compiled operator alongside the model artifacts.
mistakes.scenario_reason: Bundling the operator with model artifacts does not establish its required native runtime dependencies. A prebuilt framework image alone would leave the cause of the prediction failures unresolved.

mistakes.action: Register the working custom training image as a prediction container, and redeploy the model to the existing Agent Platform endpoint using that image unchanged.
mistakes.scenario_reason: The training image contains the dependencies, but its startup process runs training. Using it unchanged does not provide the inference server and serving interface needed for predictions.

mistakes.action: Move the model to GKE, build an inference service with the required native libraries, and operate the cluster and serving workloads through your team.
mistakes.scenario_reason: This can supply the correct runtime, but it introduces a serving migration and cluster responsibilities. Agent Platform custom prediction containers can accommodate the dependencies while retaining the existing serving infrastructure.

sources.text: Home Documentation AI and ML Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Models Send feedback Use a custom container for inference Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences. To customize how Agent Platform serves online inferences from your custom-trained model, you can specify a custom container instead of a prebuilt container when you create a Model resource. When you use a custom container, Agent Platform runs a Docker container of your choice on each inference node. You might want to use a custom container for any of the following reasons: to serve inferences from an ML model trained using a framework that isn't available as a prebuilt container to preprocess inference requests or postprocess the inferences generated by your model to run an inference server written in a programming language of your choice to install dependencies that you want to use to customize inferences This guide describes how to create a model that uses a custom container. It doesn't provide detailed instructions about designing and creating a Docker container image. Prepare a container image To create a Model that uses a custom container, you must provide a Docker container image as the basis of that container. This container image must meet the requirements described in Custom container requirements. If you plan to use an existing container image created by a third party that you trust, you might be able to skip one or both of the following sections. Create a container image Design and build a Docker container image that meets the container image requirements. To learn the basics of designing and building a Docker container image, read the Docker documentation's quickstart Push the container image to Artifact Registry Push your container image to an Artifact Registry repository. Learn how to push a container image to Artifact Registry. Create a Model To create a Model that uses a custom container, do one of the following: Import a custom-trained model. Create a TrainingPipeline that runs a CustomJob and imports the resulting artifacts as a Model. The follow sections show how to configure the API fields related to custom containers when you create a Model in one of these ways. Container-related API fields When you create the Model, make sure to configure the containerSpec field with your custom container details, rather than with a prebuilt container. You must specify a ModelContainerSpec message in the Model.containerSpec field. Within this message, you can specify the following subfields: imageUri (required) The Artifact Registry URI of your container image. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-image-uri flag to specify this field. command (optional) An array of an executable and arguments to override the container's ENTRYPOINT instruction. To learn more about how to format this field and how it interacts with the args field, read the API reference for ModelContainerSpec. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-command flag to specify this field. args (optional) An array of an executable and arguments to override the container's CMD To learn more about how to format this field and how it interacts with the command field, read the API reference for ModelContainerSpec. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-args flag to specify this field. ports (optional) An array of ports; Agent Platform sends liveness checks, health checks, and inference requests to your container on the first port listed, or 8080 by default. Specifying additional ports has no effect. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-ports flag to specify this field. env (optional) An array of environment variables that the container's ENTRYPOINT instruction, as well as the command and args fields, can reference. To learn more about how other fields can reference these environment variables, read the API reference for ModelContainerSpec. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-env-vars flag to specify this field. healthRoute (optional) The path on your container's HTTP server where you want Agent Platform to send health checks. If you don't specify this field, then when you deploy the Model as a DeployedModel to an Endpoint resource it defaults to /v1/endpoints/ENDPOINT/deployedModels/DEPLOYED_MODEL, where ENDPOINT is replaced by the last segment of the Endpoint's name field (following endpoints/) and DEPLOYED_MODEL is replaced by the DeployedModel's id field. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-health-route flag to specify this field. predictRoute (optional) The path on your container's HTTP server where you want Agent Platform to forward inference requests. If you don't specify this field, then when you deploy the Model as a DeployedModel to an Endpoint resource it defaults to /v1/endpoints/ENDPOINT/deployedModels/DEPLOYED_MODEL:predict, where ENDPOINT is replaced by the last segment of the Endpoint's name field (following endpoints/) and DEPLOYED_MODEL is replaced by the DeployedModel's id field. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-predict-route flag to specify this field. invokeRoutePrefix (optional) Invoke route prefix for the custom container. Setting this field to "/*" enables arbitrary routing for the model. Once deployed, any non-root route on the model server will be accessible with invoke HTTP call Such as, "/invoke/foo/bar" would be forwarded as "/foo/bar" to the model server. This feature is in the public preview stage. To create an invoke enabled model, follow directions to use arbitrary custom routes. sharedMemorySizeMb (optional) The amount of VM memory to reserve in a shared memory volume for the model in megabytes. Shared memory is an Inter-process communication (IPC) mechanism that allows multiple processes to access and manipulate a common block of memory. The amount of shared memory needed, if any, is an implementation detail of your container and model. Consult your model server documentation for guidelines. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-shared-memory-size-mb flag to specify this field. startupProbe (optional) Specification for the probe that checks whether the container application has started. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-startup-probe-exec, --container-startup-probe-period-seconds, --container-startup-probe-timeout-seconds flag to specify this field. healthProbe (optional) Specification for the probe that checks whether a container is ready to accept traffic. If you are using the gcloud ai models upload command, you can use the --container-health-probe-exec, --container-health-probe-period-seconds, --container-health-probe-timeout-seconds flag to specify this field. In addition to the variables that you set in the Model.containerSpec.env field, Agent Platform sets several other variables based on your configuration. Learn more about using these environment variables in these fields and in the container's ENTRYPOINT instruction. Model import examples The following examples show how to specify container-related API fields when you import a model. Note: If you use a TrainingPipeline to create a Model, you must specify these fields in a different context. You can't use the Google Cloud CLI to create a TrainingPipeline. Read more about creating custom TrainingPipeline resources. gcloud The following example uses the gcloud ai models upload command: gcloud ai models upload \ --region=LOCATION \ --display-name=MODEL_NAME \ --container-image-uri=IMAGE_URI \ --container-command=COMMAND \ --container-args=ARGS \ --container-ports=PORTS \ --container-env-vars=ENV \ --container-health-route=HEALTH_ROUTE \ --container-predict-route=PREDICT_ROUTE \ --container-shared-memory-size-mb=SHARED_MEMORY_SIZE \ --container-startup-probe-exec=STARTUP_PROBE_EXEC \ --container-startup-probe-period-seconds=STARTUP_PROBE_PERIOD \ --container-startup-probe-timeout-seconds=STARTUP_PROBE_TIMEOUT \ --container-health-probe-exec=HEALTH_PROBE_EXEC \ --container-health-probe-period-seconds=HEALTH_PROBE_PERIOD \ --container-health-probe-timeout-seconds=HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT \ --artifact-uri=PATH_TO_MODEL_ARTIFACT_DIRECTORY The --container-image-uri flag is required; all other flags that begin with --container- are optional. To learn about the values for these fields, see the preceding section of this guide. Java Before trying this sample, follow the Java setup instructions in the Agent Platform quickstart using client libraries. To authenticate to Agent Platform, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment. import com.google.api.gax.longrunning.OperationFuture; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.LocationName; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.Model; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.ModelContainerSpec; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.ModelServiceClient; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.ModelServiceSettings; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.UploadModelOperationMetadata; import com.google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.UploadModelResponse; import java.io.IOException; import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException; import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit; import java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException; public class UploadModelSample { public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException, ExecutionException, TimeoutException, IOException { // TODO(developer): Replace these variables before running the sample. String project = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"; String modelDisplayName = "YOUR_MODEL_DISPLAY_NAME"; String metadataSchemaUri = "gs://google-cloud-aiplatform/schema/trainingjob/definition/custom_task_1.0.0.yaml"; String imageUri = "YOUR_IMAGE_URI"; String artifactUri = "gs://your-gcs-bucket/artifact_path"; uploadModel(project, modelDisplayName, metadataSchemaUri, imageUri, artifactUri); } static void uploadModel( String project, String modelDisplayName, String metadataSchemaUri, String imageUri, String artifactUri) throws IOException, InterruptedException, ExecutionException, TimeoutException { ModelServiceSettings modelServiceSettings = ModelServiceSettings.newBuilder() .setEndpoint("us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com:443") .build(); // Initialize client that will be used to send requests. This client only needs to be created // once, and can be reused for multiple requests. After completing all of your requests, call // the "close" method on the client to safely clean up any remaining background resources. try (ModelServiceClient modelServiceClient = ModelServiceClient.create(modelServiceSettings)) { String location = "us-central1"; LocationName locationName = LocationName.of(project, location); ModelContainerSpec modelContainerSpec = ModelContainerSpec.newBuilder().setImageUri(imageUri).build(); Model model = Model.newBuilder() .setDisplayName(modelDisplayName) .setMetadataSchemaUri(metadataSchemaUri) .setArtifactUri(artifactUri) .setContainerSpec(modelContainerSpec) .build(); OperationFuture<UploadModelResponse, UploadModelOperationMetadata> uploadModelResponseFuture = modelServiceClient.uploadModelAsync(locationName, model); System.out.format( "Operation name: %s\n", uploadModelResponseFuture.getInitialFuture().get().getName()); System.out.println("Waiting for operation to finish..."); UploadModelResponse uploadModelResponse = uploadModelResponseFuture.get(5, TimeUnit.MINUTES); System.out.println("Upload Model Response"); System.out.format("Model: %s\n", uploadModelResponse.getModel()); } } } Node.js Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Agent Platform quickstart using client libraries. To authenticate to Agent Platform, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment. /** * TODO(developer): Uncomment these variables before running the sample.\ */ // const modelDisplayName = 'YOUR_MODEL_DISPLAY_NAME'; // const metadataSchemaUri = 'YOUR_METADATA_SCHEMA_URI'; // const imageUri = 'YOUR_IMAGE_URI'; // const artifactUri = 'YOUR_ARTIFACT_URI'; // const project = 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID'; // const location = 'YOUR_PROJECT_LOCATION'; // Imports the Google Cloud Model Service Client library const {ModelServiceClient} = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform'); // Specifies the location of the api endpoint const clientOptions = { apiEndpoint: 'us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com', }; // Instantiates a client const modelServiceClient = new ModelServiceClient(clientOptions); async function uploadModel() { // Configure the parent resources const parent = `projects/${project}/locations/${location}`; // Configure the model resources const model = { displayName: modelDisplayName, metadataSchemaUri: '', artifactUri: artifactUri, containerSpec: { imageUri: imageUri, command: [], args: [], env: [], ports: [], predictRoute: '', healthRoute: '', }, }; const request = { parent, model, }; console.log('PARENT AND MODEL'); console.log(parent, model); // Upload Model request const [response] = await modelServiceClient.uploadModel(request); console.log(`Long running operation : ${response.name}`); // Wait for operation to complete await response.promise(); const result = response.result; console.log('Upload model response '); console.log(`\tModel : ${result.model}`); } uploadModel(); Python To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Python API reference documentation. from typing import Dict, Optional, Sequence from google.cloud import aiplatform from google.cloud.aiplatform import explain def upload_model_sample( project: str, location: str, display_name: str, serving_container_image_uri: str, artifact_uri: Optional[str] = None, serving_container_predict_route: Optional[str] = None, serving_container_health_route: Optional[str] = None, description: Optional[str] = None, serving_container_command: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, serving_container_args: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, serving_container_environment_variables: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None, serving_container_ports: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None, instance_schema_uri: Optional[str] = None, parameters_schema_uri: Optional[str] = None, prediction_schema_uri: Optional[str] = None, explanation_metadata: Optional[explain.ExplanationMetadata] = None, explanation_parameters: Optional[explain.ExplanationParameters] = None, sync: bool = True, ): aiplatform.init(project=project, location=location) model = aiplatform.Model.upload( display_name=display_name, artifact_uri=artifact_uri, serving_container_image_uri=serving_container_image_uri, serving_container_predict_route=serving_container_predict_route, serving_container_health_route=serving_container_health_route, instance_schema_uri=instance_schema_uri, parameters_schema_uri=parameters_schema_uri, prediction_schema_uri=prediction_schema_uri, description=description, serving_container_command=serving_container_command, serving_container_args=serving_container_args, serving_container_environment_variables=serving_container_environment_variables, serving_container_ports=serving_container_ports, explanation_metadata=explanation_metadata, explanation_parameters=explanation_parameters, sync=sync, ) model.wait() print(model.display_name) print(model.resource_name) return model For more context, read the Model import guide. Send inference requests To send an online inference request to your Model, follow the instructions at Get inferences from a custom trained model: this process works the same regardless of whether you use a custom container. Read about predict request and response requirements for custom containers. What's next To learn about everything to consider when you design a custom container to use with Agent Platform, read Custom container requirements. Home Documentation AI and ML Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Models Send feedback Export model artifacts for inference and explanation Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform offers prebuilt containers to serve inferences and explanations from models trained using the following machine learning (ML) frameworks: TensorFlow PyTorch XGBoost scikit-learn To use one of these prebuilt containers, you must save your model as one or more model artifacts that comply with the requirements of the prebuilt container. These requirements apply whether or not your model artifacts are created on Agent Platform. If you use a custom container to serve inferences, you don't need to comply with the requirements in this page, but you can still use them as guidelines. Framework-specific requirements for exporting to prebuilt containers Depending on which ML framework you plan to use for inference, you must export model artifacts in different formats. The following sections describe the acceptable model formats for each ML framework. TensorFlow If you use TensorFlow to train a model, export your model as a TensorFlow SavedModel directory. There are several ways to export SavedModels from TensorFlow training code. The following list describes a few ways that work for various TensorFlow APIs: If you use Keras for training, use tf.keras.Model.save to export a SavedModel. If you use an Estimator for training, use tf.estimator.Estimator.export_saved_model to export a SavedModel. Otherwise, use tf.saved_model.save or use tf.compat.v1.saved_model.SavedModelBuilder. If you aren't using Keras or an Estimator, make sure to use the serve tag and serving_default signature when you export your SavedModel in order to make sure Agent Platform can use your model artifacts to serve inferences. Keras and Estimator handle this automatically. Learn more about specifying signatures during export. To serve inferences using these artifacts, create a Model with the prebuilt container for inference matching the version of TensorFlow that you used for training. TensorFlow for Vertex Explainable AI If you want to get explanations from a Model that uses a TensorFlow prebuilt container to serve inferences, read the additional requirements for exporting a TensorFlow model for Vertex Explainable AI. Enable server-side request batching for TensorFlow If you want to enable request batching for a Model that uses a TensorFlow prebuilt container to serve inferences, include config/batching_parameters_config in the same Cloud Storage directory as saved_model.pb file. To configure the batching config file, see the TensorFlow's official documentation. PyTorch You must package your model artifacts into a model archive (.mar) file. This archive must include a handler script, either default or custom, that defines how the model processes inference requests. For more advanced workflows, you should consider using custom containers instead of relying on the prebuilt PyTorch serving image. The prebuilt PyTorch images expect the archive to be named model.mar, so make sure you set the model-name to 'model' when creating the archive. For information about optimizing the memory usage, latency or throughput of a PyTorch model served with TorchServe, see the PyTorch performance guide. XGBoost If you use an XGBoost prebuilt container to train a model, you can export the trained model in the following ways: Use xgboost.Booster's save_model method to export a file named model.bst. Use the joblib library to export a file named model.joblib. Your model artifact's filename must exactly match one of these options. The following examples show how to train and export a model: Note: These examples assume that you train your model on Agent Platform and use the AIP_MODEL_DIR environment variable set by Agent Platform. xgboost.Booster import os from google.cloud import storage from sklearn import datasets import xgboost as xgb digits = datasets.load_digits() dtrain = xgb.DMatrix(digits.data, label=digits.target) bst = xgb.train({}, dtrain, 20) artifact_filename = 'model.bst' # Save model artifact to local filesystem (doesn't persist) local_path = artifact_filename bst.save_model(local_path) # Upload model artifact to Cloud Storage model_directory = os.environ['AIP_MODEL_DIR'] storage_path = os.path.join(model_directory, artifact_filename) blob = storage.blob.Blob.from_string(storage_path, client=storage.Client()) blob.upload_from_filename(local_path) joblib import os from google.cloud import storage from sklearn import datasets import joblib import xgboost as xgb digits = datasets.load_digits() dtrain = xgb.DMatrix(digits.data, label=digits.target) bst = xgb.train({}, dtrain, 20) artifact_filename = 'model.joblib' # Save model artifact to local filesystem (doesn't persist) local_path = artifact_filename joblib.dump(bst, local_path) # Upload model artifact to Cloud Storage model_directory = os.environ['AIP_MODEL_DIR'] storage_path = os.path.join(model_directory, artifact_filename) blob = storage.blob.Blob.from_string(storage_path, client=storage.Client()) blob.upload_from_filename(local_path) To serve inferences using this artifact, create a Model with the prebuilt container for inference matching the version of XGBoost that you used for training. scikit-learn If you use a scikit-learn prebuilt model to train a model, you can export it by using the joblib library to export a file named model.joblib. Your model artifact's filename must exactly match one of these options. You can export standard scikit-learn estimators or scikit-learn pipelines. The following example shows how to train and export a model: Note: These examples assume that you train your model on Agent Platform and use the AIP_MODEL_DIR environment variable set by Agent Platform. joblib import os from google.cloud import storage from sklearn import datasets from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier import joblib digits = datasets.load_digits() classifier = RandomForestClassifier() classifier.fit(digits.data, digits.target) artifact_filename = 'model.joblib' # Save model artifact to local filesystem (doesn't persist) local_path = artifact_filename joblib.dump(classifier, local_path) # Upload model artifact to Cloud Storage model_directory = os.environ['AIP_MODEL_DIR'] storage_path = os.path.join(model_directory, artifact_filename) blob = storage.blob.Blob.from_string(storage_path, client=storage.Client()) blob.upload_from_filename(local_path) To serve inferences using this artifact, create a Model with the prebuilt container for inference matching the version of scikit-learn that you used for training. What's next Read about additional requirements for your training code that you must consider when performing serverless training on Agent Platform. Learn how to create a custom TrainingPipeline resource in order to run your custom training code and create a Model from the resulting model artifacts. Learn how to import a Model from model artifacts in Cloud Storage. This applies to model artifacts that you create using a CustomJob resource or a HyperparameterTuningJob resource, as well as model artifacts that you train outside of Agent Platform.
